record.title: ALERTCalifornia cameras and AI may have helped crews rapidly detect and contain Kern County's 52-acre Trotter Fire (August 2023)
record.summary: Trotter Fire, Bear Valley Springs near Tehachapi, 14–17 August 2023, 52 acres; the AI-detection claim and “nearly 4,000 acres” counterfactual come only from ALERTCalifornia's founder via Microsoft.
record.account: Cal Fire's incident record lists the Trotter fire at Trotter Dr and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It started 14 August 2023 at 18:10 UTC under the Kern County Fire Department (not a Cal Fire incident). It burned 52 acres and was 100% contained and extinguished 17 August 2023. It says nothing about how the fire was detected or reported. KBAK (Bakersfield, 14 August 2023) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. A KGET headline the same day blamed lightning and said no homes were damaged. Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (Bruna Mori, 27 August 2026) was published after Microsoft's $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia. It included a $3 million Azure grant (announced by ALERTCalifornia on 3 February 2026). The feature says in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras and AI helped crews rapidly detect and contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. Without AI-powered imaging, ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates it may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. It quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department and deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. No fire-agency, regulator or independent news account of the fire mentions AI detection. None says which agency received the alert or its timing relative to 911 calls.

fields.account: Cal Fire's incident record lists the Trotter fire at Trotter Dr and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It started 14 August 2023 at 18:10 UTC under the Kern County Fire Department (not a Cal Fire incident). It burned 52 acres and was 100% contained and extinguished 17 August 2023. It says nothing about how the fire was detected or reported. KBAK (Bakersfield, 14 August 2023) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. A KGET headline the same day blamed lightning and said no homes were damaged. Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (Bruna Mori, 27 August 2026) was published after Microsoft's $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia. It included a $3 million Azure grant (announced by ALERTCalifornia on 3 February 2026). The feature says in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras and AI helped crews rapidly detect and contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. Without AI-powered imaging, ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates it may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. It quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department and deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. No fire-agency, regulator or independent news account of the fire mentions AI detection. None says which agency received the alert or its timing relative to 911 calls.

record.summary: 16 October 2024: AI intrusion alert and crew braking stopped 15959 Kamrup Express as about 60 elephants crossed near Lamsakhang, Assam
record.account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 pm, train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. NFR reported it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024.

fields.account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 pm, train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. NFR reported it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024.

fields.summary: 16 October 2024: AI intrusion alert and crew braking stopped 15959 Kamrup Express as about 60 elephants crossed near Lamsakhang, Assam
fields.account: On 16 October 2024 at about 8:37 pm, train 15959 Kamrup Express was running from Guwahati toward Lumding. It neared a herd of about 60 wild elephants crossing the track between Habaipur and Lamsakhang stations in Assam. Northeast Frontier Railway said loco pilot J.D. Das and assistant loco pilot Umesh Kumar noticed the herd and applied the emergency brake. It said the AI-based Intrusion Detection System operating on that section also alerted the drivers. That system uses existing optical fibers as sensors to identify animal movements and alert control offices, station masters, gatemen and loco pilots. The train stopped and no collision occurred. NFR reported it saved 414 elephants in 2023 and 383 up to 16 October 2024.

record.title: Udbetaling Danmark's fraud-control models may have produced 135, 36 and 72 cases with benefits stopped or reduced in 2023
record.summary: UDK/ATP ML fraud models (about 60 since 2019): 2023 figures of 135, 36 and 72 cases with revenue from three models; Amnesty (Nov 2024) calls their effectiveness questionable.
record.account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension). ATP designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed, established 2014 per the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database). NNIT A/S is the supplier. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes. The registry describes profiling and machine learning (it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis) run on linked register data. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls. The “Really Single” model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced). “Model Abroad” (unreported departures, state and disability pension) gave 511, 351 and 36. The parental-leave controls including the “Fictitious Employment” model gave 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. A UDK/ATP control official told Amnesty the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year, of which around 1,800 come from the models. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective. It finds most opened cases end with no further action and the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance. A Copenhagen Municipality control official said more often than not there is no fraud in the cases UDK sends. Background sources give earlier yields. AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports 2017 and 2018 controls unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments. The Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites a July 2019 report. It counted 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 in 2018 where payments were stopped, adjusted or repaid, out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. The dm.dk FOI report (October 2024) and ATP's page are not among the sources. The report said nearly all 1.2 million pensioners were screened and only 36 cases in 2023 ended with a benefit stopped or reduced. That matches the Model Abroad row. ATP's page credits 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally. The 2023 figures carry no day.

data.retained_case_account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension). ATP designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed, established 2014 per the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database). NNIT A/S is the supplier. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes. The registry describes profiling and machine learning (it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis) run on linked register data. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls. The “Really Single” model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced). “Model Abroad” (unreported departures, state and disability pension) gave 511, 351 and 36. The parental-leave controls including the “Fictitious Employment” model gave 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. A UDK/ATP control official told Amnesty the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year, of which around 1,800 come from the models. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective. It finds most opened cases end with no further action and the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance. A Copenhagen Municipality control official said more often than not there is no fraud in the cases UDK sends. Background sources give earlier yields. AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports 2017 and 2018 controls unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments. The Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites a July 2019 report. It counted 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 in 2018 where payments were stopped, adjusted or repaid, out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. The dm.dk FOI report (October 2024) and ATP's page are not among the sources. The report said nearly all 1.2 million pensioners were screened and only 36 cases in 2023 ended with a benefit stopped or reduced. That matches the Model Abroad row. ATP's page credits 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally. The 2023 figures carry no day.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The models select “requested cases” that UDK's HOK control team screens and investigates. Decisions to stop or reduce benefits are taken by humans after investigation. UDK measures model quality by the share of cases the team accepts for manual processing. Every outcome figure is a UDK statement (FOI responses and a letter) as reproduced verbatim in Amnesty International's report. No official publication of them is among the sources. Amnesty contests effectiveness and alleges discrimination risks, and UDK rejected parts of Amnesty's assessment. NNIT built the models to ATP's specifications. No developer-authored source is on record. The dm.dk report and ATP's page are not among the sources.

fields.account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension). ATP designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed, established 2014 per the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database). NNIT A/S is the supplier. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes. The registry describes profiling and machine learning (it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis) run on linked register data. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls. The “Really Single” model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced). “Model Abroad” (unreported departures, state and disability pension) gave 511, 351 and 36. The parental-leave controls including the “Fictitious Employment” model gave 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. A UDK/ATP control official told Amnesty the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year, of which around 1,800 come from the models. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective. It finds most opened cases end with no further action and the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance. A Copenhagen Municipality control official said more often than not there is no fraud in the cases UDK sends. Background sources give earlier yields. AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports 2017 and 2018 controls unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments. The Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites a July 2019 report. It counted 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 in 2018 where payments were stopped, adjusted or repaid, out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. The dm.dk FOI report (October 2024) and ATP's page are not among the sources. The report said nearly all 1.2 million pensioners were screened and only 36 cases in 2023 ended with a benefit stopped or reduced. That matches the Model Abroad row. ATP's page credits 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally. The 2023 figures carry no day.

fields.account: Udbetaling Danmark (UDK), the Danish public authority that has centralized welfare payments since 2012, has its benefits administered by ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegspension). ATP designs the fraud-control components of UDK's Joint Data Unit (Den Faelles Dataenhed, established 2014 per the University of Copenhagen's Offentlig AI database). NNIT A/S is the supplier. As of 2019 UDK was reported to use up to 60 algorithms for fraud detection and other purposes. The registry describes profiling and machine learning (it names Naive Bayes classification and cluster analysis) run on linked register data. In a letter to Amnesty International before November 2024, UDK supplied its 2023 statistics for three data-driven controls. The “Really Single” model produced 412 requested cases, 292 established control cases and 135 cases with revenue (benefits stopped or reduced). “Model Abroad” (unreported departures, state and disability pension) gave 511, 351 and 36. The parental-leave controls including the “Fictitious Employment” model gave 491, 207 and 72. UDK cautioned that cases with revenue in a year are not necessarily a proportion of cases established that year. A UDK/ATP control official told Amnesty the team manages 5,000 to 6,000 cases a year, of which around 1,800 come from the models. Amnesty's report of 12 November 2024 concludes it is questionable whether the algorithms are effective. It finds most opened cases end with no further action and the system risks discrimination and mass surveillance. A Copenhagen Municipality control official said more often than not there is no fraud in the cases UDK sends. Background sources give earlier yields. AlgorithmWatch (2020) reports 2017 and 2018 controls unveiled about half a billion kroner in erroneous payments. The Automating Society 2020 Denmark chapter cites a July 2019 report. It counted 705 cases in 2017 and 1,094 in 2018 where payments were stopped, adjusted or repaid, out of 2.7 million screened beneficiaries. The dm.dk FOI report (October 2024) and ATP's page are not among the sources. The report said nearly all 1.2 million pensioners were screened and only 36 cases in 2023 ended with a benefit stopped or reduced. That matches the Model Abroad row. ATP's page credits 260 million kr. a year of savings to IT modernization generally. The 2023 figures carry no day.

record.account: The National Audit Office (NAO) published “Tackling benefit overpayments due to fraud and error” on 22 October 2025. It states that since May 2022 the Department for Work & Pensions (DWP) has used a machine learning model. The model flags potentially fraudulent claims for Universal Credit advances. DWP estimates it saved £4.4 million from 2022–23 to 2024–25. The model scores new claims and refers those above a threshold to a caseworker. Decisions are made by DWP staff. DWP cannot disaggregate the model's costs from wider spending on data analytics. The NAO reports DWP's finding that the model is around three times more effective at identifying fraud risk than a randomized control group sample. It reports a median payment delay of one day for referred requests. DWP's July 2025 fairness analysis for 2024–25 showed older claimants (age groups 45 to 54 and above) and non-UK nationals over-referred for review. Fairness analysis was possible on only one of nine protected characteristics. Four further models were in development. Civil Service World (Jim Dunton, 22 October 2025) reported the NAO's warnings on data infrastructure. It quoted Transformation Minister Andrew Western saying that the one machine learning model has made the department significantly more effective.

fields.account: The National Audit Office (NAO) published “Tackling benefit overpayments due to fraud and error” on 22 October 2025. It states that since May 2022 the Department for Work & Pensions (DWP) has used a machine learning model. The model flags potentially fraudulent claims for Universal Credit advances. DWP estimates it saved £4.4 million from 2022–23 to 2024–25. The model scores new claims and refers those above a threshold to a caseworker. Decisions are made by DWP staff. DWP cannot disaggregate the model's costs from wider spending on data analytics. The NAO reports DWP's finding that the model is around three times more effective at identifying fraud risk than a randomized control group sample. It reports a median payment delay of one day for referred requests. DWP's July 2025 fairness analysis for 2024–25 showed older claimants (age groups 45 to 54 and above) and non-UK nationals over-referred for review. Fairness analysis was possible on only one of nine protected characteristics. Four further models were in development. Civil Service World (Jim Dunton, 22 October 2025) reported the NAO's warnings on data infrastructure. It quoted Transformation Minister Andrew Western saying that the one machine learning model has made the department significantly more effective.

fields.account: The National Audit Office (NAO) published “Tackling benefit overpayments due to fraud and error” on 22 October 2025. It states that since May 2022 the Department for Work & Pensions (DWP) has used a machine learning model. The model flags potentially fraudulent claims for Universal Credit advances. DWP estimates it saved £4.4 million from 2022–23 to 2024–25. The model scores new claims and refers those above a threshold to a caseworker. Decisions are made by DWP staff. DWP cannot disaggregate the model's costs from wider spending on data analytics. The NAO reports DWP's finding that the model is around three times more effective at identifying fraud risk than a randomized control group sample. It reports a median payment delay of one day for referred requests. DWP's July 2025 fairness analysis for 2024–25 showed older claimants (age groups 45 to 54 and above) and non-UK nationals over-referred for review. Fairness analysis was possible on only one of nine protected characteristics. Four further models were in development. Civil Service World (Jim Dunton, 22 October 2025) reported the NAO's warnings on data infrastructure. It quoted Transformation Minister Andrew Western saying that the one machine learning model has made the department significantly more effective.

record.account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010–11. Its annual report calls it an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated an average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield. It was about £4.6 billion in 2024–25, with around 4,300 staff using it. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024–25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment). It served to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation. IDRS replaced it from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.

fields.account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010–11. Its annual report calls it an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated an average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield. It was about £4.6 billion in 2024–25, with around 4,300 staff using it. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024–25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment). It served to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation. IDRS replaced it from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.

fields.account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010–11. Its annual report calls it an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated an average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield. It was about £4.6 billion in 2024–25, with around 4,300 staff using it. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024–25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment). It served to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation. IDRS replaced it from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.

record.title: Independent evaluation finds Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts skillful beyond four days in Mali's frequently flooded regions, suggesting seven-day Red Cross early-action triggers
record.summary: Forecasts could allow earlier action in parts of Mali, but Google Flood Hub produced frequent false alarms. No benefit from an implemented early action was measured.
record.account: Researchers evaluated Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts against river-flow observations and records of flood impacts in Mali. Their results suggest that some early-action plans could extend from four to seven days without much loss of forecast skill. Performance varied across districts and thresholds, and no correctly predicted floods were found in the northern districts that were evaluated. At a seven-day lead time, Google Flood Hub’s false-alarm ratio was around 0.8 across discharge thresholds, compared with around 0.5 for GloFAS. The authors describe GloFAS as more balanced in several comparisons. They used a ten-day matching window to compare forecasts with reported impacts, which affects the interpretation of performance. This was a retrospective forecast evaluation; it did not measure benefits from an implemented early action. The researchers are independent of Google, although one coauthor works at the Joint Research Centre, which contributes to GloFAS.

fields.account: Researchers evaluated Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts against river-flow observations and records of flood impacts in Mali. Their results suggest that some early-action plans could extend from four to seven days without much loss of forecast skill. Performance varied across districts and thresholds, and no correctly predicted floods were found in the northern districts that were evaluated. At a seven-day lead time, Google Flood Hub’s false-alarm ratio was around 0.8 across discharge thresholds, compared with around 0.5 for GloFAS. The authors describe GloFAS as more balanced in several comparisons. They used a ten-day matching window to compare forecasts with reported impacts, which affects the interpretation of performance. This was a retrospective forecast evaluation; it did not measure benefits from an implemented early action. The researchers are independent of Google, although one coauthor works at the Joint Research Centre, which contributes to GloFAS.

fields.account: ECMWF announced that on 25 February 2025 it began producing operational forecasts with AIFS Single, the deterministic version of its Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System. It claimed tropical cyclone track gains of up to 20%. ECMWF's evaluation of 2025 forecasts (8 May 2026) reports AIFS errors 5 to 15% lower than the IFS for most surface and upper-air variables. Cyclone position was substantially better but intensity under-predicted. NHC's Science Operations Officer said ECMWF's AI-driven global system was available for evaluation at NHC during the 2025 season. No specific event in which AIFS beat the IFS is documented in the ECMWF cited sources. The Severe Event Catalog page for Storm Eowyn states wind gusts were not available for AIFS.

record.summary: CIRA/Colorado State evaluation: GraphCast and three AI models match top operational cyclone track models in 2023; adding all four cut consensus error 11% at 120 h.
record.account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on ECMWF's public charts from 2023. DeepMind's blog of 14 November 2023 says the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. The blog says only “In September”, so the year is implied by its 14 November 2023 post date. The ECMWF publications read do not document the case. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben saying the models are so good they cannot be avoided. An independent CIRA/Colorado State evaluation applied NHC verification to May-November 2023 cyclones. It found GraphCast-operational and three other AI models' track errors comparable to the best operational models. Adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h.

MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben saying the models are so good they cannot be avoided. It found GraphCast-operational and three other AI models' track errors comparable to the best operational models. Adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h.

fields.account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on ECMWF's public charts from 2023. DeepMind's blog of 14 November 2023 says the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. The blog says only “In September”, so the year is implied by its 14 November 2023 post date. The ECMWF publications read do not document the case. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben saying the models are so good they cannot be avoided. An independent CIRA/Colorado State evaluation applied NHC verification to May-November 2023 cyclones. It found GraphCast-operational and three other AI models' track errors comparable to the best operational models. Adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h.

record.title: A GraphCast live run on ECMWF charts may have forecast Hurricane Lee's Nova Scotia landfall about nine days ahead
record.summary: DeepMind says a live GraphCast run on ECMWF's site forecast Lee's Nova Scotia landfall about nine days ahead; NHC records landfall 16 September 2023; no forecaster use of the run is documented.
record.account: Google DeepMind's blog post of 14 November 2023 describes a live version of its publicly available GraphCast model, deployed on the ECMWF website. In September 2023 it predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. MIT Technology Review (14 November 2023) relayed the claim from DeepMind staff research scientist Rémi Lam. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The article quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. ECMWF's Newsletter 177 editorial (Autumn 2023) confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on ECMWF's public charts pages from ECMWF's own initial conditions. The NHC tropical cyclone report on Lee (21 March 2024) records the landfall. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Maximum sustained winds were about 55 kt. NHC official track errors were exceptionally low through 72 h and below five-year means through 120 h. The report mentions no AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast is on record, and the NHC 2023 verification report contains no AI-model entry. It found only an intensity-structure mention of Lee in the independent CIRA preprint. The forecast itself is dated only as “September” by the vendor. No cited source documents a forecaster or authority acting on the GraphCast Lee run.

later.note: An independent Uppsala University evaluation published 7 November 2024 confirmed GraphCast's general advantage over ECMWF's IFS HRES, including on near-surface temperature and wind extremes; it does not examine the Hurricane Lee forecast, and the NHC's March 2024 report on Lee names no AI model.

data.retained_case_account: Google DeepMind's blog post of 14 November 2023 describes a live version of its publicly available GraphCast model, deployed on the ECMWF website. In September 2023 it predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. MIT Technology Review (14 November 2023) relayed the claim from DeepMind staff research scientist Rémi Lam. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The article quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. ECMWF's Newsletter 177 editorial (Autumn 2023) confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on ECMWF's public charts pages from ECMWF's own initial conditions. The NHC tropical cyclone report on Lee (21 March 2024) records the landfall. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Maximum sustained winds were about 55 kt. NHC official track errors were exceptionally low through 72 h and below five-year means through 120 h. The report mentions no AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast is on record, and the NHC 2023 verification report contains no AI-model entry. It found only an intensity-structure mention of Lee in the independent CIRA preprint. The forecast itself is dated only as “September” by the vendor. No cited source documents a forecaster or authority acting on the GraphCast Lee run.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The only sources for the nine-day Lee forecast are the maker's own blog and a news report quoting the maker's scientist. ECMWF's editorial confirms only that GraphCast ran experimentally on its charts. NHC's Lee report records exceptionally low official track errors without mentioning AI guidance. The AI output is therefore documented as a forecast, not as an input to any decision.

fields.summary: DeepMind says a live GraphCast run on ECMWF's site forecast Lee's Nova Scotia landfall about nine days ahead; NHC records landfall 16 September 2023; no forecaster use of the run is documented.
fields.account: Google DeepMind's blog post of 14 November 2023 describes a live version of its publicly available GraphCast model, deployed on the ECMWF website. In September 2023 it predicted about nine days in advance that Hurricane Lee would make landfall in Nova Scotia. MIT Technology Review (14 November 2023) relayed the claim from DeepMind staff research scientist Rémi Lam. It added that traditional forecasting models pinpointed Nova Scotia only six days in advance. The article quotes no ECMWF staff on Lee. ECMWF's Newsletter 177 editorial (Autumn 2023) confirms that GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet were made available on ECMWF's public charts pages from ECMWF's own initial conditions. The NHC tropical cyclone report on Lee (21 March 2024) records the landfall. Lee, by then post-tropical, made landfall on Long Island in southwestern Nova Scotia around 2000 UTC on 16 September 2023. Maximum sustained winds were about 55 kt. NHC official track errors were exceptionally low through 72 h and below five-year means through 120 h. The report mentions no AI model. No ECMWF document recording the Lee forecast is on record, and the NHC 2023 verification report contains no AI-model entry. It found only an intensity-structure mention of Lee in the independent CIRA preprint. The forecast itself is dated only as “September” by the vendor. No cited source documents a forecaster or authority acting on the GraphCast Lee run.

record.title: Randomized evaluation of Google AI flood alerts with community dissemination in Bihar, India (2022–2023 monsoons)
record.summary: Bihar RCT, 319 panchayats: households relayed Google flood alerts reported 16.6% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical costs.
record.account: Google's AI flood-forecasting system, run with India's Central Water Commission (CWC), issues riverine flood alerts as Android push notifications. In Bihar, India, economists Maulik Jagnani (Tufts) and Rohini Pande (Yale) ran a randomized evaluation across 319 panchayats in 12 flood-prone districts. It covered the 2022 and 2023 monsoon seasons (June to October). The non-governmental organization Yuganter trained community volunteers to relay the alerts. Treatment households got 2.41 more alerts in 2022 and were 46.5% more likely to get an alert before water reached their area. They reported 16.56% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical spending than controls. No specific evacuation tied to an alert is documented.
record.purpose: The forecasting system was built to warn people of riverine floods before water arrives so they can prepare or evacuate. The measured preparedness and health effects are that intended benefit, but only at cohort level.

data.retained_case_account: Google's AI flood-forecasting system, run with India's Central Water Commission (CWC), issues riverine flood alerts as Android push notifications. In Bihar, India, economists Maulik Jagnani (Tufts) and Rohini Pande (Yale) ran a randomized evaluation across 319 panchayats in 12 flood-prone districts. It covered the 2022 and 2023 monsoon seasons (June to October). The non-governmental organization Yuganter trained community volunteers to relay the alerts. Treatment households got 2.41 more alerts in 2022 and were 46.5% more likely to get an alert before water reached their area. They reported 16.56% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical spending than controls. No specific evacuation tied to an alert is documented.

record.title: IdentiFlight automated curtailment at Top of the World cuts the eagle fatality rate by an estimated 50–82%, with wide uncertainty
record.summary: Peregrine Fund, WEST and USGS researchers estimated an 82% (75%–89%) relative cut in eagle deaths at a Wyoming wind farm after IdentiFlight curtailment; a 2023 reanalysis put it at 50% (−159%, 89%).
record.account: McClure et al. (Journal of Applied Ecology, Crossref publication date 31 January 2021) tested an automated curtailment system. The site was Top of the World Windpower Facility, Wyoming, USA. Authors are from The Peregrine Fund, Western EcoSystems Technology and the U.S. Geological Survey. The cameras detect and classify flying objects and decide whether to curtail individual turbines. The design was before–after–control–impact, with a control site 15 km away. Correcting for carcass detection probability, they estimated fatalities fell 63% at the treatment site (95% confidence interval, CI, 59%–66%). They rose 113% at the control site, an 82% (75%–89%) relative reduction. They noted fatalities were not eliminated. Recharge reported the claim on 28 January 2021. Huso and Dalthorp (Journal of Applied Ecology, 30 August 2023) reanalyzed the data and reported four major errors. Corrected, these give 50% (−159%, 89%), consistent with no effect. McClure et al. replied the same day that their data support the efficacy of automated curtailment. Duerr et al. (PLoS One, 26 January 2023) assessed an IdentiFlight installation in California. It correctly identified 77% of eagles and 85% of non-eagles, with 5,439 curtailment orders for non-eagle targets against 850 for eagles. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor logged the 82% result as a positive record.

comparator.quote: After correcting for carcass detection probability and scaling fatality estimates to turbine‐years, we estimate that the number of fatalities at the treatment site declined by 63% (95% CI = 59%–66%) between before and after periods while increasing at the control site by 113% (51%–218%). later.note: A USGS reanalysis by Huso and Dalthorp found the 82% claim unsupported, estimating a 50% reduction with an interval spanning an increase; the original authors published a rebuttal the same day.

data.retained_case_account: McClure et al. (Journal of Applied Ecology, Crossref publication date 31 January 2021) tested an automated curtailment system. The site was Top of the World Windpower Facility, Wyoming, USA. Authors are from The Peregrine Fund, Western EcoSystems Technology and the U.S. Geological Survey. The cameras detect and classify flying objects and decide whether to curtail individual turbines. The design was before–after–control–impact, with a control site 15 km away. Correcting for carcass detection probability, they estimated fatalities fell 63% at the treatment site (95% confidence interval, CI, 59%–66%). They rose 113% at the control site, an 82% (75%–89%) relative reduction. They noted fatalities were not eliminated. Recharge reported the claim on 28 January 2021. Huso and Dalthorp (Journal of Applied Ecology, 30 August 2023) reanalyzed the data and reported four major errors. Corrected, these give 50% (−159%, 89%), consistent with no effect. McClure et al. replied the same day that their data support the efficacy of automated curtailment. Duerr et al. (PLoS One, 26 January 2023) assessed an IdentiFlight installation in California. It correctly identified 77% of eagles and 85% of non-eagles, with 5,439 curtailment orders for non-eagle targets against 850 for eagles. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor logged the 82% result as a positive record.

fields.account: McClure et al. (Journal of Applied Ecology, Crossref publication date 31 January 2021) tested an automated curtailment system. The site was Top of the World Windpower Facility, Wyoming, USA. Authors are from The Peregrine Fund, Western EcoSystems Technology and the U.S. Geological Survey. The cameras detect and classify flying objects and decide whether to curtail individual turbines. The design was before–after–control–impact, with a control site 15 km away. Correcting for carcass detection probability, they estimated fatalities fell 63% at the treatment site (95% confidence interval, CI, 59%–66%). They rose 113% at the control site, an 82% (75%–89%) relative reduction. They noted fatalities were not eliminated. Recharge reported the claim on 28 January 2021. Huso and Dalthorp (Journal of Applied Ecology, 30 August 2023) reanalyzed the data and reported four major errors. Corrected, these give 50% (−159%, 89%), consistent with no effect. McClure et al. replied the same day that their data support the efficacy of automated curtailment. Duerr et al. (PLoS One, 26 January 2023) assessed an IdentiFlight installation in California. It correctly identified 77% of eagles and 85% of non-eagles, with 5,439 curtailment orders for non-eagle targets against 850 for eagles. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor logged the 82% result as a positive record.

fields.summary: Peregrine Fund, WEST and USGS researchers estimated an 82% (75%–89%) relative cut in eagle deaths at a Wyoming wind farm after IdentiFlight curtailment; a 2023 reanalysis put it at 50% (−159%, 89%).
fields.account: McClure et al. (Journal of Applied Ecology, Crossref publication date 31 January 2021) tested an automated curtailment system. The site was Top of the World Windpower Facility, Wyoming, USA. Authors are from The Peregrine Fund, Western EcoSystems Technology and the U.S. Geological Survey. The cameras detect and classify flying objects and decide whether to curtail individual turbines. The design was before–after–control–impact, with a control site 15 km away. Correcting for carcass detection probability, they estimated fatalities fell 63% at the treatment site (95% confidence interval, CI, 59%–66%). They rose 113% at the control site, an 82% (75%–89%) relative reduction. They noted fatalities were not eliminated. Recharge reported the claim on 28 January 2021. Huso and Dalthorp (Journal of Applied Ecology, 30 August 2023) reanalyzed the data and reported four major errors. Corrected, these give 50% (−159%, 89%), consistent with no effect. McClure et al. replied the same day that their data support the efficacy of automated curtailment. Duerr et al. (PLoS One, 26 January 2023) assessed an IdentiFlight installation in California. It correctly identified 77% of eagles and 85% of non-eagles, with 5,439 curtailment orders for non-eagle targets against 850 for eagles. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor logged the 82% result as a positive record.

record.title: A CIA tool called “Ghost Murmur”, pairing quantum magnetometry with AI, may have located downed F-15E officer “Dude 44 Bravo” in Iran before his 4 April 2026 rescue
record.summary: The rescue is documented. The claim that Ghost Murmur located the airman rests on two anonymous sources and a subsequent presidential remark; its technical capability remains unverified.
record.account: The April 6 White House briefing documents the rescue of the downed F-15E weapons systems officer in Iran. The official transcript also describes watching his suspected position with a camera from 40 miles away. That distance concerns the camera, not an established heartbeat-detection range. On April 7, the New York Post reported that two anonymous sources attributed the officer's location to a CIA tool called Ghost Murmur. They described quantum magnetic sensing combined with AI that separates a heartbeat signal from background noise, and attributed its development to Lockheed Martin's Skunk Works. Lockheed Martin declined to comment. In an April 8 telephone interview with the Post, President Trump called the tool important to the rescue, but supplied no technical explanation. The Post and Scientific American separately interviewed physicists who questioned the described capability. The official briefing does not name Ghost Murmur or establish an AI contribution. No public measurements or inspectable technical account establish that the claimed system located the officer.

fields.account: The April 6 White House briefing documents the rescue of the downed F-15E weapons systems officer in Iran. The official transcript also describes watching his suspected position with a camera from 40 miles away. That distance concerns the camera, not an established heartbeat-detection range. On April 7, the New York Post reported that two anonymous sources attributed the officer's location to a CIA tool called Ghost Murmur. They described quantum magnetic sensing combined with AI that separates a heartbeat signal from background noise, and attributed its development to Lockheed Martin's Skunk Works. Lockheed Martin declined to comment. In an April 8 telephone interview with the Post, President Trump called the tool important to the rescue, but supplied no technical explanation. The Post and Scientific American separately interviewed physicists who questioned the described capability. The official briefing does not name Ghost Murmur or establish an AI contribution. No public measurements or inspectable technical account establish that the claimed system located the officer.

fields.summary: The rescue is documented. The claim that Ghost Murmur located the airman rests on two anonymous sources and a subsequent presidential remark; its technical capability remains unverified.
fields.account: The April 6 White House briefing documents the rescue of the downed F-15E weapons systems officer in Iran. The official transcript also describes watching his suspected position with a camera from 40 miles away. That distance concerns the camera, not an established heartbeat-detection range. On April 7, the New York Post reported that two anonymous sources attributed the officer's location to a CIA tool called Ghost Murmur. They described quantum magnetic sensing combined with AI that separates a heartbeat signal from background noise, and attributed its development to Lockheed Martin's Skunk Works. Lockheed Martin declined to comment. In an April 8 telephone interview with the Post, President Trump called the tool important to the rescue, but supplied no technical explanation. The Post and Scientific American separately interviewed physicists who questioned the described capability. The official briefing does not name Ghost Murmur or establish an AI contribution. No public measurements or inspectable technical account establish that the claimed system located the officer.

record.title: Meta self-harm alert routed to Uttar Pradesh Police leads to hospital treatment of a 25-year-old in Meerut within eight minutes
record.summary: 7 June 2026: Meta alert at 6:53 pm; Meerut police reached a 25-year-old in 8 minutes, found him critical; hospital treatment, improved
record.account: On 7 June 2026 a 25-year-old man from the Sardhana area of Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, posted an Instagram video. In it he appeared to drink a white liquid. Police said Meta sent a suicide alert about the post to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters at 6:53 pm. The center alerted Meerut Police, and a Sardhana team reached his home within eight minutes. They found him in a critical condition with a bottle of suspected liquid nearby and took him to hospital, where his condition improved after treatment. He told police he was under stress following the end of a relationship. Police data cited by PTI credit such alerts with 3,011 lives saved statewide from 1 January 2023 to 31 May 2026.

data.retained_case_account: On 7 June 2026 a 25-year-old man from the Sardhana area of Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, posted an Instagram video. In it he appeared to drink a white liquid. Police said Meta sent a suicide alert about the post to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters at 6:53 pm. The center alerted Meerut Police, and a Sardhana team reached his home within eight minutes. They found him in a critical condition with a bottle of suspected liquid nearby and took him to hospital, where his condition improved after treatment. He told police he was under stress following the end of a relationship. Police data cited by PTI credit such alerts with 3,011 lives saved statewide from 1 January 2023 to 31 May 2026.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Police sources say Meta sent the alert after the post. They do not state whether Meta's classifier or a user report flagged it. Meta's documentation and NPR describe the process as machine-learning detection with human review before contacting authorities. The record relies on that description and should be read with that caveat.

fields.account: On 7 June 2026 a 25-year-old man from the Sardhana area of Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, posted an Instagram video. In it he appeared to drink a white liquid. Police said Meta sent a suicide alert about the post to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters at 6:53 pm. The center alerted Meerut Police, and a Sardhana team reached his home within eight minutes. They found him in a critical condition with a bottle of suspected liquid nearby and took him to hospital, where his condition improved after treatment. He told police he was under stress following the end of a relationship. Police data cited by PTI credit such alerts with 3,011 lives saved statewide from 1 January 2023 to 31 May 2026.

record.account: On 29 March 2026 an 18-year-old class 12 student from Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, texted his girlfriend “Alvida” after a breakup. He lived within the Mill Area police station limits. He also posted a suicide video on Instagram with rat poison and messages of intent. At about 8:58 pm Meta flagged the content and emailed an alert to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters. The center traced his mobile number and location and alerted Raebareli police. A police team reached his home within 12 minutes and found him in severe distress, with an empty rat-poison packet nearby. Police and family took him to a nearby hospital, where he was treated. On 1 April 2026 police said he was stable.

data.retained_case_account: On 29 March 2026 an 18-year-old class 12 student from Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, texted his girlfriend “Alvida” after a breakup. He lived within the Mill Area police station limits. He also posted a suicide video on Instagram with rat poison and messages of intent. At about 8:58 pm Meta flagged the content and emailed an alert to the Social Media Center at Uttar Pradesh Police headquarters. The center traced his mobile number and location and alerted Raebareli police. A police team reached his home within 12 minutes and found him in severe distress, with an empty rat-poison packet nearby. Police and family took him to a nearby hospital, where he was treated. On 1 April 2026 police said he was stable.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Police say Meta flagged the Instagram post at about 8:58 pm on 29 March and emailed the Uttar Pradesh Police Social Media Center. No source says whether Meta's classifier or a user report started the review. Decode reports that UP alerts arise from “artificial intelligence systems or user reports” reviewed by Meta staff. Everything after the email was human work. The center traced the phone number and location. Raebareli police reached the home in 12 minutes on the DGP's instructions, and a hospital treated him.

record.title: HSI's Operation Renewed Hope uses facial recognition and AI image enhancement to identify 311 probable child victims in cold cases
record.summary: A three-week HSI-led surge from 17 Jul 2023 produced 311 probable identifications of unknown child victims, 14 positive contacts and several rescues; officials credit facial recognition and AI images.
record.account: The operation began on 17 July 2023 and ended in early August. HSI's Cyber Crimes Center hosted investigators from the FBI, U.S. Marshals, Interpol, Europol and 13 foreign agencies to review unidentified child sexual abuse material series. ICE reports 311 probable identifications of previously unknown victims, 14 positive contacts and several confirmed rescues from active abuse. Over 100 leads went to field offices and 25 countries, with arrests already made in the United States and Canada. NBC News reports that HSI officials credited new facial recognition and artificial intelligence technology for fresh leads. Mike Prado of HSI described AI- or machine-learning-enhanced images as a starting point for investigation. ABC (Australia) reports that the operation used Clearview AI's facial recognition alongside other techniques, citing Queensland Police analyst Scott Anderson. Forbes reports that officials did not confirm Clearview or any specific program. The ICE release itself does not mention AI.

data.retained_case_account: The operation began on 17 July 2023 and ended in early August. HSI's Cyber Crimes Center hosted investigators from the FBI, U.S. Marshals, Interpol, Europol and 13 foreign agencies to review unidentified child sexual abuse material series. ICE reports 311 probable identifications of previously unknown victims, 14 positive contacts and several confirmed rescues from active abuse. Over 100 leads went to field offices and 25 countries, with arrests already made in the United States and Canada. NBC News reports that HSI officials credited new facial recognition and artificial intelligence technology for fresh leads. Mike Prado of HSI described AI- or machine-learning-enhanced images as a starting point for investigation. ABC (Australia) reports that the operation used Clearview AI's facial recognition alongside other techniques, citing Queensland Police analyst Scott Anderson. Forbes reports that officials did not confirm Clearview or any specific program. The ICE release itself does not mention AI.

record.account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer, bank, country, date, regulator or court record is given for any case, and none was found. The page is the vendor's own account.

data.retained_case_account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer, bank, country, date, regulator or court record is given for any case, and none was found. The page is the vendor's own account.

fields.account: Vyntra's “Fraud Cases” page was published 4 April 2022 per its page metadata; the cases themselves are undated. It states that “Our solutions stop the fraud before the money leaves the bank” and lists about two dozen short case studies at unnamed banks. One is an account takeover after pharming stopped before a CHF 19,990 payment. Another is an impersonation that led a bank employee to validate a CHF 1,000,000 transaction, blocked because the beneficiary was unusual at bank level. There are vishing, tech-support, CEO-fraud, business-email-compromise, romance and invoice-redirection cases. Their payments of EUR 22,114, EUR 33,170, USD 7,500, GBP 21,000, EUR 125,000, EUR 170,000, USD 100,000, USD 170,000 and USD 850,000 were stopped. Transaction or e-banking session variables (beneficiary, country, amount, currency, browser, screen resolution, language) did not match the customer's or bank's usual profile. There are two internal-fraud cases. In one case “fraudsters were arrested while attempting to withdraw USD 500,000 (KSh 58 million) from the second bank's ATMs”. The models had flagged unusual timing and frequency of withdrawals. One entry still names “NetGuardians solution”, the Swiss company that merged with Belgium's Intix to form Vyntra in June 2025 (FinTech Global, 19 June 2025). No customer, bank, country, date, regulator or court record is given for any case, and none was found. The page is the vendor's own account.

details.label: Purpose
details.value: ASENA (Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı) is the Turkish National Police's narcotics analysis software, in service since March 2021. Built to flag and investigate drug crime from integrated police and justice databases. The Hakkari flag was worked as a suspected drug shipment and the search found explosives instead, so this benefit was outside the system's design purpose.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: The program supplied the lead and nothing more. The minister said the analysis programs, “what they call artificial intelligence”, had identified a suspicious vehicle thought to be carrying drugs. The Hakkari police chief called him on the evening of 20 March. Officers then stopped the car at a fixed checkpoint, searched the concealed compartment and arrested the driver; prosecutors and the court did the rest. No source describes the program's inputs, the data it matched, or whether an analyst reviewed the flag before the stop. record.summary: Police analysis software flagged a car at Yüksekova on 20 March 2022; it held 52.5 kg of explosives officials said were bound for Istanbul.
record.account: On 20 March 2022 at about 19:00, officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at the Yüksekova-Van checkpoint exit in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged it as suspicious, initially as a suspected drug shipment. A search of a hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well found 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive assessed as PETN-RDX. The driver, A.K., a police officer posted in Istanbul, was remanded on 22 March 2022. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March that the target was Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court gave A.K. 21 years for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. Four co-defendants got 17.5 years each.
record.purpose: ASENA (Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı) is the Turkish National Police's narcotics analysis software, in service since March 2021. Built to flag and investigate drug crime from integrated police and justice databases. The Hakkari flag was worked as a suspected drug shipment and the search found explosives instead, so this benefit was outside the system's design purpose.

fields.account: On 20 March 2022 at about 19:00, officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at the Yüksekova-Van checkpoint exit in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged it as suspicious, initially as a suspected drug shipment. A search of a hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well found 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive assessed as PETN-RDX. The driver, A.K., a police officer posted in Istanbul, was remanded on 22 March 2022. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March that the target was Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court gave A.K. 21 years for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. Four co-defendants got 17.5 years each.

fields.summary: Police analysis software flagged a car at Yüksekova on 20 March 2022; it held 52.5 kg of explosives officials said were bound for Istanbul.
fields.account: On 20 March 2022 at about 19:00, officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at the Yüksekova-Van checkpoint exit in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged it as suspicious, initially as a suspected drug shipment. A search of a hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well found 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive assessed as PETN-RDX. The driver, A.K., a police officer posted in Istanbul, was remanded on 22 March 2022. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March that the target was Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court gave A.K. 21 years for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. Four co-defendants got 17.5 years each.

record.title: WeChat Pay's “anti-fraud customer service reminder” interrupts a Yunnan man's 190,000 yuan transfer to a suspected romance scammer, and he cancels the payment (14 December 2021)
record.summary: WeChat says its anti-fraud reminder, with Tencent Cloud online service, led a Yunnan man to cancel a 190,000 yuan transfer to a “goddess” he had met online; reported by ChinaZ, 14 December 2021.
record.account: According to WeChat (ChinaZ, 14 December 2021; ZOL, 16 December 2021), WeChat Pay launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder”. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button and the system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. ChinaZ reports that a Mr. Zhang in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. The customer service, judging from experience that this looked like a dating scam, explained the pattern and advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. The Monitor bundles this with Shanghai police figures for 2021 (115,000 scam calls blocked daily; 510 million yuan directly recovered). Xinmin attributes those to police, the communications administration and carriers without naming AI.

data.retained_case_account: According to WeChat (ChinaZ, 14 December 2021; ZOL, 16 December 2021), WeChat Pay launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder”. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button and the system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. ChinaZ reports that a Mr. Zhang in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. The customer service, judging from experience that this looked like a dating scam, explained the pattern and advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. The Monitor bundles this with Shanghai police figures for 2021 (115,000 scam calls blocked daily; 510 million yuan directly recovered). Xinmin attributes those to police, the communications administration and carriers without naming AI.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The automated part the sources describe is the flagging of a risky transaction. That triggers the on-screen reminder and connects the payer to Tencent Cloud Zhifu, a service the Monitor calls AI. ChinaZ says the WeChat Pay customer service judged “from experience” that this was a dating scam, which reads as a human agent. Neither report says how the transaction was flagged or whether any model was involved. The advice, not the flag alone, led Zhang to cancel.

fields.summary: WeChat says its anti-fraud reminder, with Tencent Cloud online service, led a Yunnan man to cancel a 190,000 yuan transfer to a “goddess” he had met online; reported by ChinaZ, 14 December 2021.
fields.account: According to WeChat (ChinaZ, 14 December 2021; ZOL, 16 December 2021), WeChat Pay launched an “anti-fraud customer service reminder”. When a payment is flagged as a risky transaction, the screen shows an “answer the reminder” button and the system connects automatically. Tencent Cloud Zhifu then provides online customer service to help judge the risk. ChinaZ reports that a Mr. Zhang in Yunnan had met a woman on a video platform. Within a week she asked to borrow 190,000 yuan for medical treatment. As he initiated the transfer, a WeChat Pay voice reminder appeared. The customer service, judging from experience that this looked like a dating scam, explained the pattern and advised him to cancel. He avoided a loss of 190,000 yuan. The Monitor bundles this with Shanghai police figures for 2021 (115,000 scam calls blocked daily; 510 million yuan directly recovered). Xinmin attributes those to police, the communications administration and carriers without naming AI.

record.summary: In April 2019 a California officer ran a NCMEC missing-child photo through Thorn's Spotlight; Rekognition matching returned sex ads with the girl and, per Thorn's CEO, she was recovered within weeks.
record.account: The source places the case in April 2019 without a day. Thorn CEO Julie Cordua, speaking at an Amazon conference, was quoted by WIRED's Tom Simonite. She said a California law enforcement officer screenshotted a missing child's picture from a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children post. The officer ran it through Spotlight, Thorn's investigator tool that matches faces and other clues in online sex ads. Using Amazon's facial recognition, Spotlight returned a list of ads featuring the girl, who had been sold for weeks. More traditional police work followed and, she said, the child was recovered within weeks. Snopes notes Thorn's 2017 impact report claimed its tools helped identify 5,791 child victims and rescue 103. The figures are from Thorn's surveys of police users, and viral claims conflated identification with rescue. No police or court record of this case is among the sources.

data.retained_case_account: The source places the case in April 2019 without a day. Thorn CEO Julie Cordua, speaking at an Amazon conference, was quoted by WIRED's Tom Simonite. She said a California law enforcement officer screenshotted a missing child's picture from a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children post. The officer ran it through Spotlight, Thorn's investigator tool that matches faces and other clues in online sex ads. Using Amazon's facial recognition, Spotlight returned a list of ads featuring the girl, who had been sold for weeks. More traditional police work followed and, she said, the child was recovered within weeks. Snopes notes Thorn's 2017 impact report claimed its tools helped identify 5,791 child victims and rescue 103. The figures are from Thorn's surveys of police users, and viral claims conflated identification with rescue. No police or court record of this case is among the sources.

fields.summary: In April 2019 a California officer ran a NCMEC missing-child photo through Thorn's Spotlight; Rekognition matching returned sex ads with the girl and, per Thorn's CEO, she was recovered within weeks.
fields.account: The source places the case in April 2019 without a day. Thorn CEO Julie Cordua, speaking at an Amazon conference, was quoted by WIRED's Tom Simonite. She said a California law enforcement officer screenshotted a missing child's picture from a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children post. The officer ran it through Spotlight, Thorn's investigator tool that matches faces and other clues in online sex ads. Using Amazon's facial recognition, Spotlight returned a list of ads featuring the girl, who had been sold for weeks. More traditional police work followed and, she said, the child was recovered within weeks. Snopes notes Thorn's 2017 impact report claimed its tools helped identify 5,791 child victims and rescue 103. The figures are from Thorn's surveys of police users, and viral claims conflated identification with rescue. No police or court record of this case is among the sources.

The system did not predict a crime or act on its own. The warrants, the arrest and the evidence-gathering were police and court actions. OpenAI sent only the user's prompts, not ChatGPT's replies. What the assistant said to the user, and whether it helped or hindered him, is unknown.

record.title: OpenAI alert relayed through the FBI leads Espírito Santo police to detain a father a day before his stated date to kill his son
record.summary: OpenAI flagged a user's plan to kill his 8-year-old son; relayed via the FBI, Brazilian police held him a day before his stated date.
record.account: In 2026 a 36-year-old farmer in São Gabriel da Palha, Espírito Santo, Brazil, told ChatGPT about a plan to kill his 8-year-old son. He said he had offered R$50,000 to a hitman and set 20 June as the date. OpenAI's safety systems flagged the account, and the company referred it to the FBI. The FBI passed it to the Ministry of Justice's CyberLab. The Polícia Civil received it on 16 June and, under warrants, arrested him on 19 June. Officers seized his phone, four bottles of an unidentified substance and a knotted rope. He admitted the searches but denied intent. He was freed on habeas corpus on 13 August 2026 after 54 days, under an ankle monitor and a no-contact order. The inquiry continues.
record.purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant. OpenAI's moderation layer is built to route conversations that indicate plans to harm others to human reviewers. Those reviewers may refer an imminent threat to law enforcement, under a policy published 26 August 2025. The referral that triggered the arrest was that layer doing what it was built to do, not an emergent use of the assistant.

data.retained_case_account: In 2026 a 36-year-old farmer in São Gabriel da Palha, Espírito Santo, Brazil, told ChatGPT about a plan to kill his 8-year-old son. He said he had offered R$50,000 to a hitman and set 20 June as the date. OpenAI's safety systems flagged the account, and the company referred it to the FBI. The FBI passed it to the Ministry of Justice's CyberLab. The Polícia Civil received it on 16 June and, under warrants, arrested him on 19 June. Officers seized his phone, four bottles of an unidentified substance and a knotted rope. He admitted the searches but denied intent. He was freed on habeas corpus on 13 August 2026 after 54 days, under an ankle monitor and a no-contact order. The inquiry continues.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: OpenAI's automated classifiers and human reviewers flagged the user's messages, and the company chose to refer the account to the FBI. The system did not predict a crime or act on its own. The warrants, the arrest and the evidence-gathering were police and court actions. OpenAI sent only the user's prompts, not ChatGPT's replies. What the assistant said to the user, and whether it helped or hindered him, is unknown.

fields.account: In 2026 a 36-year-old farmer in São Gabriel da Palha, Espírito Santo, Brazil, told ChatGPT about a plan to kill his 8-year-old son. He said he had offered R$50,000 to a hitman and set 20 June as the date. OpenAI's safety systems flagged the account, and the company referred it to the FBI. The FBI passed it to the Ministry of Justice's CyberLab. The Polícia Civil received it on 16 June and, under warrants, arrested him on 19 June. Officers seized his phone, four bottles of an unidentified substance and a knotted rope. He admitted the searches but denied intent. He was freed on habeas corpus on 13 August 2026 after 54 days, under an ankle monitor and a no-contact order. The inquiry continues.

record.title: Saronic Corsair sea drone picks up two Apache crew off Oman and carries them to a helicopter hoist
record.summary: A Navy Corsair sea drone picked up two Apache crew off Oman and carried them to a helicopter hoist; CENTCOM reported that both were rescued within about two hours.
record.account: U.S. Central Command reported that two Army AH-64 Apache crew members were rescued at 7:33 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026, or 3:33 a.m. on June 9 in Oman. That is the rescue time, not the time that the helicopter went down. CENTCOM said that recovery took approximately two hours and that both crew members were stable. In a direct interview with DefenseScoop, Capt. Tim Hawkins identified the vessel as a Saronic Corsair operated by the Navy’s Task Force 59. He said that it picked up the crew and carried them to another point on the water for a helicopter hoist. The official release said that the cause of the helicopter’s loss was under investigation. The sources do not identify which autonomous functions were used during the rescue.

data.retained_case_account: U.S. Central Command reported that two Army AH-64 Apache crew members were rescued at 7:33 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026, or 3:33 a.m. on June 9 in Oman. That is the rescue time, not the time that the helicopter went down. CENTCOM said that recovery took approximately two hours and that both crew members were stable. In a direct interview with DefenseScoop, Capt. Tim Hawkins identified the vessel as a Saronic Corsair operated by the Navy’s Task Force 59. He said that it picked up the crew and carried them to another point on the water for a helicopter hoist. The official release said that the cause of the helicopter’s loss was under investigation. The sources do not identify which autonomous functions were used during the rescue.

fields.account: U.S. Central Command reported that two Army AH-64 Apache crew members were rescued at 7:33 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026, or 3:33 a.m. on June 9 in Oman. That is the rescue time, not the time that the helicopter went down. CENTCOM said that recovery took approximately two hours and that both crew members were stable. In a direct interview with DefenseScoop, Capt. Tim Hawkins identified the vessel as a Saronic Corsair operated by the Navy’s Task Force 59. He said that it picked up the crew and carried them to another point on the water for a helicopter hoist. The official release said that the cause of the helicopter’s loss was under investigation. The sources do not identify which autonomous functions were used during the rescue.

record.title: Asilla's behavior-analysis AI at about 40 Japanese stations and buildings may have prompted two suicide interventions
record.summary: Asilla told Kyodo that camera alerts prompted guards to intervene in two apparent suicide risks. The facilities and dates were not identified, and the company is the sole source of those accounts.
record.account: The two interventions are undated. Tokyo-based Asilla's system assesses the likelihood that a person will jump by analyzing behavior on security-camera footage. It looks for behavior such as pacing or lingering near a platform edge or rooftop. It alerts security guards and station staff, in some cases with loudspeaker warnings. In one case it detected a man loitering in a non-customer area of a commercial facility. A guard found him, and he later said he had intended to kill himself by jumping. In another, a child lingering near an upper-floor railing was found to have been writing a suicide note. Asilla says it trained the system since 2022 with around 200 facilities on about seven million pieces of footage. All details come from the company via Kyodo, and no operator, police or academic confirmation is among the sources. data.retained_case_account: The two interventions are undated. Tokyo-based Asilla's system assesses the likelihood that a person will jump by analyzing behavior on security-camera footage. It looks for behavior such as pacing or lingering near a platform edge or rooftop. It alerts security guards and station staff, in some cases with loudspeaker warnings. In one case it detected a man loitering in a non-customer area of a commercial facility. A guard found him, and he later said he had intended to kill himself by jumping. In another, a child lingering near an upper-floor railing was found to have been writing a suicide note. Asilla says it trained the system since 2022 with around 200 facilities on about seven million pieces of footage. All details come from the company via Kyodo, and no operator, police or academic confirmation is among the sources. Asilla’s earlier product release identifies a jump-risk detection function in AI Security asilla version 2.4, using movement trajectories, position, and body-motion patterns. It does not identify the version used in these two interventions.

fields.account: The two interventions are undated. Tokyo-based Asilla's system assesses the likelihood that a person will jump by analyzing behavior on security-camera footage. It looks for behavior such as pacing or lingering near a platform edge or rooftop. It alerts security guards and station staff, in some cases with loudspeaker warnings. In one case it detected a man loitering in a non-customer area of a commercial facility. A guard found him, and he later said he had intended to kill himself by jumping. In another, a child lingering near an upper-floor railing was found to have been writing a suicide note. Asilla says it trained the system since 2022 with around 200 facilities on about seven million pieces of footage. All details come from the company via Kyodo, and no operator, police or academic confirmation is among the sources. Asilla’s earlier product release identifies a jump-risk detection function in AI Security asilla version 2.4, using movement trajectories, position, and body-motion patterns. It does not identify the version used in these two interventions.

record.account: Court reporting describes an OpenAI emergency disclosure that reached the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office through the FBI after Darren Zhou wrote threats against his ex-girlfriend in ChatGPT. Deputies compared those messages with anonymous threats that she had preserved. The sheriff’s booking entry lists May 29, 2026 as his arrest date. BocaNewsNow reports that he pleaded guilty on August 13 to written threats, aggravated stalking, and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Adjudication was withheld, with eight years of probation, two years of GPS monitoring, and restrictions on contact and weapons. The accessible reporting cites court documents but does not reproduce the complete affidavit or plea order. It supports a police intervention and court restrictions, rather than proof that an attack would otherwise have occurred.
