details.label: Purpose
details.value: Autoland exists to take complete control of an aircraft and land it when the pilot cannot fly. It engages on its own when cabin altitude exceeds a set level. That is what happened here. The two pilots turned out not to be incapacitated, though, and chose to let it finish.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: Autoland engaged itself when cabin altitude exceeded the limit. It declared the emergency to controllers with automated “pilot incapacitation” broadcasts. It flew the descent, approach and landing. The pilots elected to leave it engaged rather than take over. So the landing is the system's work. But the counterfactual, that they could not have landed, is not established. Garmin, the FAA and the operator all call it an automated system. None calls it AI. It is here because the OECD Monitor lists it as an AI system. The Register describes it choosing landing sites from runway length, distance and fuel range.

record.title: Garmin Autoland engages after a King Air B200 loses cabin pressure at 23,000 ft and lands it at Broomfield, Colorado, in its first real emergency use
record.summary: On 20 December 2025 Garmin Autoland flew a depressurised King Air B200 to a landing at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport; two pilots unhurt.
record.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 ft it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. The crew chose to leave it engaged. Nobody was treated. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it was investigating and the NTSB that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and six news reports. The Monitor dates the event 22 December 2025; every report puts the landing on Saturday 20 December, which is used here. Early reports (AVweb, Denver7, ABC's headline) said the pilot was incapacitated; the operator's CEO, quoted by CBS, ABC and The Register, says the system engaged on cabin-altitude exceedance and the crew were not incapacitated. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented because the crew were conscious and elected to leave the system engaged, so no counterfactual is established. Aircraft type is given as Super King Air 200 (ABC, Denver7) and King Air B200 (AVweb, The Register). The Monitor's General Aviation News and FOX31 follow-up links returned HTTP 403, AVweb's “crew decision” piece returned 404, and the Independent blocked fetching, so its Yahoo syndication is cited. Garmin's Autonomí pages returned only navigation, so no vendor source is cited; Garmin's statements are quoted via the news reports.
Benefit type set to Increased Product Safety under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

fields.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 ft it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. The crew chose to leave it engaged. Nobody was treated. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it was investigating and the NTSB that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and six news reports. The Monitor dates the event 22 December 2025; every report puts the landing on Saturday 20 December, which is used here. Early reports (AVweb, Denver7, ABC's headline) said the pilot was incapacitated; the operator's CEO, quoted by CBS, ABC and The Register, says the system engaged on cabin-altitude exceedance and the crew were not incapacitated. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented because the crew were conscious and elected to leave the system engaged, so no counterfactual is established. Aircraft type is given as Super King Air 200 (ABC, Denver7) and King Air B200 (AVweb, The Register). The Monitor's General Aviation News and FOX31 follow-up links returned HTTP 403, AVweb's “crew decision” piece returned 404, and the Independent blocked fetching, so its Yahoo syndication is cited. Garmin's Autonomí pages returned only navigation, so no vendor source is cited; Garmin's statements are quoted via the news reports.
Benefit type set to Increased Product Safety under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

Controllers and ground services act on the automated broadcasts, as Broomfield's two fire departments did.

fields.summary: On 20 December 2025 Garmin Autoland flew a depressurised King Air B200 to a landing at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport; two pilots unhurt.
fields.account: On Saturday 20 December 2025 Buffalo River Aviation's Beechcraft Super King Air B200, N479BR, left Aspen-Pitkin County Airport at 1:43 p.m. It carried two pilots and no passengers. At about 23,000 ft it suffered a rapid, uncommanded loss of pressurization. When cabin altitude passed the safe limit, Garmin Autoland engaged automatically. It sent automated emergency broadcasts to air traffic control. It flew the aircraft to a landing on Runway 30 at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport, Broomfield, Colorado, shortly after 2 p.m. The crew chose to leave it engaged. Nobody was treated. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it was investigating and the NTSB that it was gathering information. Garmin called it the first use of Autoland from start to finish in an actual emergency.

details.value: Hanoi's AI traffic-camera system has 1,837 cameras with AI-controlled signals and was due to enter official operation in December 2025, per VOV. The Traffic Police run it, in VOV's words, “to ensure security and order and support the people” as well as to manage traffic. Tracing a lost resident for a ward police search falls within that stated remit.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: The system's contribution was the trace. Police searched it in the direction the family gave. It returned images of the man walking along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and across other streets. That gave the police a route and pictures for a public appeal. A passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng about eleven hours after the report. No source says the finder had seen the appeal or that officers reached him. So the discovery itself is not attributable to the system. The vendor is not named and every account comes from the police.

record.title: Hanoi traffic police trace a missing 78-year-old on the city's new AI camera network; a passer-by finds him hypoglycemic in Dịch Vọng at 3 a.m.
record.summary: Hanoi police traced a lost 78-year-old on AI traffic cameras on 15 December 2025; a passer-by found him at 3 a.m. the next day and took him home.
record.account: Mr Đ.V.T., 78, of Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025 and did not return. At 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department. Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team there searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction the family gave. It traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets. VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng, hypoglycemic and close to fainting, and took him home. No source links the finder to the appeal.

data.retained_case_account: Mr Đ.V.T., 78, of Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025 and did not return. At 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department. Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team there searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction the family gave. It traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets. VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng, hypoglycemic and close to fainting, and took him home. No source links the finder to the appeal.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The system's contribution was the trace. Police searched it in the direction the family gave. It returned images of the man walking along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and across other streets. That gave the police a route and pictures for a public appeal. A passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng about eleven hours after the report. No source says the finder had seen the appeal or that officers reached him. So the discovery itself is not attributable to the system. The vendor is not named and every account comes from the police.

record.title: UNEP MARS notification leads an operator to stop a 1,200-tonne methane pipeline leak in Kazakhstan (KAZ_S_136); IMEO observed emissions at the site again by May 2026
record.summary: UNEP IMEO case KAZ_S_136: pipeline leak first detected Sept 2025, operator rerouted gas, mitigation reported 26 Nov 2025, last emissions 12 Mar 2026; subsequent emissions seen as of 21 May 2026.
record.account: UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) publishes a Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) case document for source KAZ_S_136. It is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. The document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by DLR's EnMAP on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. Last emissions were detected on 12 March 2026 (document updated 15 April 2026). A footnote states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments and companies. The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP's snapshot, counts one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed Kazakhstan gas-pipeline mitigation of an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither gives a case ID, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established.

data.retained_case_account: UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) publishes a Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) case document for source KAZ_S_136. It is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. The document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by DLR's EnMAP on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. Last emissions were detected on 12 March 2026 (document updated 15 April 2026). A footnote states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments and companies. The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP's snapshot, counts one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed Kazakhstan gas-pipeline mitigation of an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither gives a case ID, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established.

fields.account: UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) publishes a Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) case document for source KAZ_S_136. It is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. The document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by DLR's EnMAP on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. Last emissions were detected on 12 March 2026 (document updated 15 April 2026). A footnote states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments and companies. The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP's snapshot, counts one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed Kazakhstan gas-pipeline mitigation of an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither gives a case ID, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established.

fields.account: UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) publishes a Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) case document for source KAZ_S_136. It is an oil-and-gas pipeline in Kazakhstan at 43.39767°, 52.49505°. The document gives coordinates only. The document records first detection in September 2025, a plume imaged by DLR's EnMAP on 29 October 2025 and estimated emissions of 1,200 tonnes. The operator transferred the gas flow from the affected pipeline to another pipeline, stopping the emissions. Mitigation was reported on 26 November 2025. Last emissions were detected on 12 March 2026 (document updated 15 April 2026). A footnote states that as of 21 May 2026 IMEO observed subsequent methane emissions at the location and continues to engage stakeholders. UNEP's MARS page states that IMEO uses data from more than 30 satellite instruments coupled with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. It uses them to notify governments and companies. The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP's snapshot, counts one Kazakhstan source among six that stopped emitting in 2026 after MARS alerts. UNEP's September 2026 snapshot reports a confirmed Kazakhstan gas-pipeline mitigation of an estimated 365 tonnes over one month. Neither gives a case ID, so their correspondence to KAZ_S_136 is not established.

record.account: The reports arrived from mid-September 2025. Stenberg writes that a security report received on 16 September accurately identified a possible stack-based buffer overflow in curl's Kerberos FTP code. It was not turned into a CVE only because the code could not be reached. The project then removed krb5-ftp support. The reporter, Joshua Rogers, then forwarded a large list of further potential issues found mostly with ZeroPath, an AI-powered code analyzer. That produced over two hundred possible problems despite curl's existing compilers, static analyzers and fuzzing. From the initial list about 50 separately identifiable bugfixes were merged. Second and third lists of 47 and 158 items followed. Stenberg told The Register that about 50 bugfixes based on Rogers' reports had been merged. Rogers' retrospective states that about 98% of the curl bugs reported and fixed were discovered by ZeroPath. It puts the running total of fixed bugs around 150.

fields.account: The reports arrived from mid-September 2025. Stenberg writes that a security report received on 16 September accurately identified a possible stack-based buffer overflow in curl's Kerberos FTP code. It was not turned into a CVE only because the code could not be reached. The project then removed krb5-ftp support. The reporter, Joshua Rogers, then forwarded a large list of further potential issues found mostly with ZeroPath, an AI-powered code analyzer. That produced over two hundred possible problems despite curl's existing compilers, static analyzers and fuzzing. From the initial list about 50 separately identifiable bugfixes were merged. Second and third lists of 47 and 158 items followed. Stenberg told The Register that about 50 bugfixes based on Rogers' reports had been merged. Rogers' retrospective states that about 98% of the curl bugs reported and fixed were discovered by ZeroPath. It puts the running total of fixed bugs around 150.

fields.account: The reports arrived from mid-September 2025. Stenberg writes that a security report received on 16 September accurately identified a possible stack-based buffer overflow in curl's Kerberos FTP code. It was not turned into a CVE only because the code could not be reached. The project then removed krb5-ftp support. The reporter, Joshua Rogers, then forwarded a large list of further potential issues found mostly with ZeroPath, an AI-powered code analyzer. That produced over two hundred possible problems despite curl's existing compilers, static analyzers and fuzzing. From the initial list about 50 separately identifiable bugfixes were merged. Second and third lists of 47 and 158 items followed. Stenberg told The Register that about 50 bugfixes based on Rogers' reports had been merged. Rogers' retrospective states that about 98% of the curl bugs reported and fixed were discovered by ZeroPath. It puts the running total of fixed bugs around 150.

fields.account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day, automated and unstaffed outside normal hours. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. Dates, recovered goods and any police statement are not reported.

fields.summary: AI cameras in Szeged's unstaffed-at-night Coop flagged a shopper hiding goods; police caught them within hours, the operators said.
fields.account: Coop Szeged Zrt. and Laurel Kft. opened the 247 Shop on Szent István tér in Szeged at the end of May 2025. It is staffed by day, automated and unstaffed outside normal hours. Cameras running the French company Veesion's software analyze shoppers' movements without identifying faces. They alert a remote dispatch service to gestures such as concealing goods. On 9 October 2025 the operators issued a press release relayed by Index.hu and MTI. It said over four and a half months the system had exposed three theft attempts. In one, a person hid products under their clothing during night mode. Police caught the perpetrator within hours using the footage. Dates, recovered goods and any police statement are not reported.

record.title: Google's Big Sleep agent may have isolated SQLite CVE-2025–6965 from threat-intel artifacts; fixed in 3.50.2 before exploitation
record.summary: Google says Big Sleep, fed indicators that attackers were staging a zero-day, isolated SQLite CVE-2025–6965; SQLite shipped the fix in 3.50.2 on 28 June 2025, announced 15 July 2025.
record.account: The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. The CVE record was published 15 July 2025. Google's post says that, based on intel from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. It was at risk of being exploited, the post says. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. Big Sleep was used to isolate it, the spokesperson said. Google declined to name the actors or describe the indicators. The CVE record, assigned by Google, credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. Independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent is absent. The claim rests on Google.

fields.account: The SQLite 3.50.2 release carrying the fix is dated 28 June 2025. The CVE record was published 15 July 2025. Google's post says that, based on intel from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. It was at risk of being exploited, the post says. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. Big Sleep was used to isolate it, the spokesperson said. Google declined to name the actors or describe the indicators. The CVE record, assigned by Google, credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. Independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent is absent. The claim rests on Google.

Google's post says that, based on intel from Google Threat Intelligence, the Big Sleep agent discovered an SQLite vulnerability known only to threat actors. It was at risk of being exploited, the post says. A Google spokesperson told The Record that its threat intelligence group found artifacts indicating a zero-day was being staged but could not identify the vulnerability. Big Sleep was used to isolate it, the spokesperson said. Google declined to name the actors or describe the indicators. The CVE record, assigned by Google, credits Vlad Stolyarov of Google's Threat Analysis Group with assistance from Google Big Sleep. SQLite's release log lists the corresponding fix. Independent confirmation that exploitation was imminent is absent. The claim rests on Google.

record.title: South Wales Police's Operator Initiated Facial Recognition app identifies a 38-year-old in Cardiff wanted on a 2012 European arrest warrant from Poland; he is remanded to Westminster magistrates
record.summary: A South Wales Police officer's OIFR phone app matched a 38-year-old in Cardiff to a 2012 Polish European arrest warrant for drug dealing and assaulting an officer; he was remanded (July 2025).
record.account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone and compare the image with a reference database. It is for when the person refuses or gives false details. It launched in December 2024. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing and assaulting a police officer with a weapon in Poland. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The forces report 50 South Wales searches producing 10 arrests, and six Gwent uses with three matches and one arrest. They cite National Physical Laboratory testing in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The arrest date is not given.

fields.account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone and compare the image with a reference database. It is for when the person refuses or gives false details. It launched in December 2024. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing and assaulting a police officer with a weapon in Poland. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The forces report 50 South Wales searches producing 10 arrests, and six Gwent uses with three matches and one arrest. They cite National Physical Laboratory testing in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The arrest date is not given.

fields.account: South Wales Police and Gwent Police are the first UK forces with the Operator Initiated Facial Recognition (OIFR) app. It lets an officer photograph a person on a police phone and compare the image with a reference database. It is for when the person refuses or gives false details. It launched in December 2024. More than 500 officers had been trained by July 2025 (Emergency Services Times, 15 July 2025). In one use, an officer in Cardiff identified a 38-year-old man wanted on a European arrest warrant since 2012. The warrant was for drug dealing and assaulting a police officer with a weapon in Poland. He was remanded in custody to Westminster magistrates' court (Wales Online, 14 July 2025). The forces report 50 South Wales searches producing 10 arrests, and six Gwent uses with three matches and one arrest. They cite National Physical Laboratory testing in which the correct match came top for people in the database (Wales Online). The arrest date is not given.

record.summary: Diário de Cuiabá (14 July 2025): Sesp-MT's Vigia Mais MT cameras matched a woman with a June 2024 trafficking warrant in central Cuiabá on 12 July; Ciosp tracked her live and the 1st BPM arrested her.
record.account: On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest a woman in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. She had an open warrant for drug trafficking. That is per the same text carried by Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento on 14 July and CliqueF5 on 15 July 2025. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. It passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. Her warrant had been issued on 19 June 2024 by the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. The reports add that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located and arrested by state security forces.

fields.account: On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest a woman in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. She had an open warrant for drug trafficking. That is per the same text carried by Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento on 14 July and CliqueF5 on 15 July 2025. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. It passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. Her warrant had been issued on 19 June 2024 by the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. The reports add that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located and arrested by state security forces.

fields.account: On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest a woman in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. She had an open warrant for drug trafficking. That is per the same text carried by Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento on 14 July and CliqueF5 on 15 July 2025. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. It passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. Her warrant had been issued on 19 June 2024 by the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. The reports add that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located and arrested by state security forces.

details.label: Focus
details.value: Public and environmental security

details.label: Purpose
details.value: The EPB introduced AI smoke-recognition cameras in 2022 to recognize abnormal smoke around the clock at open-burning hotspots. They send automatic alerts so inspectors can locate and stop pollution sources and reduce fire risk. Detecting and recording this roadside burning was that intended use.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: The AI smoke-recognition system and micro-sensors supplied the detection that sent inspectors to the burning site. CNA dates it first to 4 July 2025, then repeatedly in July and August. It also supplied the video that recorded the offender. It could not read his faded motorcycle plate. So identification came from private CCTV, dashcam footage and a police officer's recognition of a local resident. The system's contribution is detection and documentation. Removal of the source depended on human investigation. No measured air-quality change or proven counterfactual is reported. So the record sits at protective response with prevention unproven rather than specific harm prevented.

record.title: Taichung EPB's AI smoke-recognition system catches a serial roadside waste burner in Dadu District
record.summary: Taichung EPB AI smoke detection flagged roadside waste burning in Dadu District; a 74-year-old repeat offender was caught and fined.
record.account: Taichung's Environmental Protection Bureau (EPB) installed its AI smoke-recognition system, air micro-sensors and cameras beside Hugan Road, Dadu District. That followed a March 2025 complaint about smoke from a dumping spot. CNA reports that shortly after 08:00 on 4 July 2025 the instruments flagged abnormal air quality. Inspectors found dumped waste burning. The system recorded the same man in July and August. His motorcycle plate was too faded to read. So inspectors collected neighbors' closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage. A Wuri Precinct officer recognized a 74-year-old man surnamed Zhao, who confessed. On 13 September 2025 the EPB announced a fine of up to NT$100,000 under the Air Pollution Control Act. It asked the land manager to clear the site.
record.purpose: The EPB introduced AI smoke-recognition cameras in 2022 to recognize abnormal smoke around the clock at open-burning hotspots. They send automatic alerts so inspectors can locate and stop pollution sources and reduce fire risk. Detecting and recording this roadside burning was that intended use.
record.system: AI智慧判煙系統 (AI smart smoke-recognition system) with air micro-sensors and surveillance cameras, operated by the Taichung City Environmental Protection Bureau; 36 hotspot monitoring stations as of July 2025 and over 100 AI and sensor sites citywide by September 2025
record.deployer: Taichung City Government Environmental Protection Bureau (臺中市政府環境保護局)
record.taxonomy_note: An illegal burner caught and fined removes a pollution source; no air-quality change is measured.

ratings.reason: The EPB says the case removed “a potential pollution source threatening air quality” for residents near Hugan Road in Dadu District. CTS and PTS describe repeated burns at the same spot in February, July and August 2025 next to weeds. No exposure figures or air-quality measurements are reported. So the benefit is material but local and unquantified.

The EPB and Wuri Precinct police closed a repeat-offender case that the faded plate had stalled. The system's alert and video supplied the inspection trigger and the core evidence. The EPB presents the case as proof that its “smart technology city” enforcement works.

data.retained_case_account: Taichung's Environmental Protection Bureau (EPB) installed its AI smoke-recognition system, air micro-sensors and cameras beside Hugan Road, Dadu District. That followed a March 2025 complaint about smoke from a dumping spot. CNA reports that shortly after 08:00 on 4 July 2025 the instruments flagged abnormal air quality. Inspectors found dumped waste burning. The system recorded the same man in July and August. His motorcycle plate was too faded to read. So inspectors collected neighbors' closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage. A Wuri Precinct officer recognized a 74-year-old man surnamed Zhao, who confessed. On 13 September 2025 the EPB announced a fine of up to NT$100,000 under the Air Pollution Control Act. It asked the land manager to clear the site.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The AI smoke-recognition system and micro-sensors supplied the detection that sent inspectors to the burning site. CNA dates it first to 4 July 2025, then repeatedly in July and August. It also supplied the video that recorded the offender. It could not read his faded motorcycle plate. So identification came from private CCTV, dashcam footage and a police officer's recognition of a local resident. The system's contribution is detection and documentation. Removal of the source depended on human investigation. No measured air-quality change or proven counterfactual is reported. So the record sits at protective response with prevention unproven rather than specific harm prevented.

fields.account: Taichung's Environmental Protection Bureau (EPB) installed its AI smoke-recognition system, air micro-sensors and cameras beside Hugan Road, Dadu District. That followed a March 2025 complaint about smoke from a dumping spot. CNA reports that shortly after 08:00 on 4 July 2025 the instruments flagged abnormal air quality. Inspectors found dumped waste burning. The system recorded the same man in July and August. His motorcycle plate was too faded to read. So inspectors collected neighbors' closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage. A Wuri Precinct officer recognized a 74-year-old man surnamed Zhao, who confessed. On 13 September 2025 the EPB announced a fine of up to NT$100,000 under the Air Pollution Control Act. It asked the land manager to clear the site.

ratings.reason: The EPB says the case removed “a potential pollution source threatening air quality” for residents near Hugan Road in Dadu District. CTS and PTS describe repeated burns at the same spot in February, July and August 2025 next to weeds. No exposure figures or air-quality measurements are reported. So the benefit is material but local and unquantified.

The EPB and Wuri Precinct police closed a repeat-offender case that the faded plate had stalled. The system's alert and video supplied the inspection trigger and the core evidence. The EPB presents the case as proof that its “smart technology city” enforcement works.

produced_by: Fixed AI smoke-recognition cameras and air micro-sensors installed at a known open-burning hotspot after a public complaint, with automatic alerts to inspectors
Inspectors able to reach the site while the fire burned. They could assemble third-party CCTV and dashcam footage when its video could not read the faded plate
Local police (Wuri Precinct Dadu Station) familiar enough with residents to match the recorded build, clothing and gait to a known 74-year-old resident
A legal basis for penalties (Air Pollution Control Act Article 32) and a land manager that could be asked to clear the dump site
must_hold: The AI alert must reach staff who can respond while the fire is burning and who have the mandate to enter the site
Identification must not rest on the camera alone. Plate recognition failed here and human evidence-gathering closed the case
The offender must be identifiable and reachable. A stranger with no local ties would likely not have been recognized

fields.summary: Taichung EPB AI smoke detection flagged roadside waste burning in Dadu District; a 74-year-old repeat offender was caught and fined.
fields.account: Taichung's Environmental Protection Bureau (EPB) installed its AI smoke-recognition system, air micro-sensors and cameras beside Hugan Road, Dadu District. That followed a March 2025 complaint about smoke from a dumping spot. CNA reports that shortly after 08:00 on 4 July 2025 the instruments flagged abnormal air quality. Inspectors found dumped waste burning. The system recorded the same man in July and August. His motorcycle plate was too faded to read. So inspectors collected neighbors' closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage. A Wuri Precinct officer recognized a 74-year-old man surnamed Zhao, who confessed. On 13 September 2025 the EPB announced a fine of up to NT$100,000 under the Air Pollution Control Act. It asked the land manager to clear the site.

record.title: Met Police live facial recognition flags David Cheneler, a sex offender breaching his order, alone with a six-year-old girl and a lock knife at Denmark Hill
record.summary: Met LFR flagged David Cheneler, 73, with a six-year-old and a lock knife at Denmark Hill, Jan 2025, breaching his SOPO; jailed 20 May 2025.
record.account: In January 2025 Metropolitan Police Live Facial Recognition (LFR) cameras on a van at Denmark Hill identified David Cheneler, 73. He was under a 2019 Sexual Offences Prevention Order barring him from being alone with children under 14. The order followed a 2010 conviction for 15 counts of indecent assault on a female under 16 and five of gross indecency with a child. Officers found him with a six-year-old girl he had collected from school for her mother. The mother did not know his history. A lock knife was hidden in his belt buckle. He pleaded guilty at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on 13 January 2025 to breaching the order and possessing an offensive weapon. On 20 May 2025 Kingston Crown Court jailed him for two years.
record.purpose: The Met deploys Live Facial Recognition cameras on police vans to identify people of interest and alert officers. Its LFR lead, Lindsey Chiswick, describes the aim as using data and technology to identify offenders that pose a risk to our communities. Identifying a sex offender in breach of his order was that purpose.

produced_by: A van-mounted LFR deployment at Denmark Hill in January 2025 and a face the system was able to identify. The match alerted officers on the spot.
Officers who stopped him at once and found the child and the lock knife hidden in his belt buckle. They knew the terms of his 2019 Sexual Offences Prevention Order.
A court record of the order and his 2010 convictions. This turned the stop into a guilty plea for breaching the order and possessing an offensive weapon.
must_hold: The person must be known to the system and subject to conditions that make his presence with a child an offense. The benefit depends on the prior order, not on the camera alone.
Officers must verify the match and intervene immediately. The child was found only because he was stopped on the spot.

The deployment must be lawful and proportionate. The OECD Monitor files this same event under human-rights, psychological, reputational and public-interest harm types. The protective benefit therefore sits beside a contested surveillance practice.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Dated 20 May 2025, the sentencing at Kingston Crown Court and the Monitor's own date; the LFR identification happened in January 2025 (Southwark News), before his guilty plea at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on Monday 13 January 2025, and no readable source gives the day. Country of the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.

data.retained_case_account: In January 2025 Metropolitan Police Live Facial Recognition (LFR) cameras on a van at Denmark Hill identified David Cheneler, 73. He was under a 2019 Sexual Offences Prevention Order barring him from being alone with children under 14. The order followed a 2010 conviction for 15 counts of indecent assault on a female under 16 and five of gross indecency with a child. Officers found him with a six-year-old girl he had collected from school for her mother. The mother did not know his history. A lock knife was hidden in his belt buckle. He pleaded guilty at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on 13 January 2025 to breaching the order and possessing an offensive weapon. On 20 May 2025 Kingston Crown Court jailed him for two years.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The LFR system did the identification. Cameras on the back of a van at Denmark Hill matched Cheneler's face and alerted officers, Southwark News reports. Finding the child and the knife, the arrest, the charges and the sentence were human and judicial acts. The offense itself existed only because of his 2019 order. The counterfactual is the Met's own hedge. DC Adam Pearce said it is possible that, had he not been identified, Cheneler could have gone on to abuse the child. No allegation about this occasion is reported. The readable source does not name the vendor or algorithm. The Met's press release is not among the sources.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Dated 20 May 2025, the sentencing at Kingston Crown Court and the Monitor's own date; the LFR identification happened in January 2025 (Southwark News), before his guilty plea at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on Monday 13 January 2025, and no readable source gives the day. Of the Monitor's eleven sources only Southwark News could be read: BBC, Sky News, The Times, Daily Mail, Mirror, The Irish Sun, Daily Star and News Shopper are not fetchable by this tool, the London News Online and Parikiaki pages are gone, and the Met newsroom search did not render, so the Met's press release was not read and the vendor and algorithm are not named. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented because the Met's own officer put the averted abuse as possible and no allegation about this occasion is reported.
Benefit type set to Reduced Violence under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since from the cited sources.

fields.account: In January 2025 Metropolitan Police Live Facial Recognition (LFR) cameras on a van at Denmark Hill identified David Cheneler, 73. He was under a 2019 Sexual Offences Prevention Order barring him from being alone with children under 14. The order followed a 2010 conviction for 15 counts of indecent assault on a female under 16 and five of gross indecency with a child. Officers found him with a six-year-old girl he had collected from school for her mother. The mother did not know his history. A lock knife was hidden in his belt buckle. He pleaded guilty at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on 13 January 2025 to breaching the order and possessing an offensive weapon. On 20 May 2025 Kingston Crown Court jailed him for two years.

record.title: OpenAI o3 finds CVE-2025–37899, a remote use-after-free in the Linux kernel's ksmbd; patched in all maintained branches
record.summary: Sean Heelan, benchmarking o3 on ksmbd with no scaffolding, had the model surface an unknown use-after-free in the SMB logoff handler; the kernel CNA published CVE-2025–37899 on 20 May 2025.
record.account: Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher auditing ksmbd (the Linux kernel's in-kernel SMB3 server). He used a known bug (CVE-2025–37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 via the plain application programming interface (API), with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. The Linux kernel CNA's record describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches. Linuxiac reports the upstream response was fast and patches were merged for every maintained branch. Heelan calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model (LLM) finding a vulnerability of that nature.

data.retained_case_account: Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher auditing ksmbd (the Linux kernel's in-kernel SMB3 server). He used a known bug (CVE-2025–37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 via the plain application programming interface (API), with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. The Linux kernel CNA's record describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches. Linuxiac reports the upstream response was fast and patches were merged for every maintained branch. Heelan calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model (LLM) finding a vulnerability of that nature.

fields.summary: Sean Heelan, benchmarking o3 on ksmbd with no scaffolding, had the model surface an unknown use-after-free in the SMB logoff handler; the kernel CNA published CVE-2025–37899 on 20 May 2025.
fields.account: Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher auditing ksmbd (the Linux kernel's in-kernel SMB3 server). He used a known bug (CVE-2025–37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 via the plain application programming interface (API), with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. The Linux kernel CNA's record describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches. Linuxiac reports the upstream response was fast and patches were merged for every maintained branch. Heelan calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model (LLM) finding a vulnerability of that nature.

record.title: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras locate a white BMW that had been roaring down Jieshou Road at night, within a day of residents' complaint
record.summary: Taoyuan's AI sound cameras pinpointed a white BMW noise car the day after residents complained; officers caught it on 23 April 2025.
record.account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.

data.retained_case_account: Residents of Bade District, Taoyuan, complained in the Facebook group 記憶八德. A white BMW with a loud exhaust kept roaring down Jieshou Road late at night. The Taoyuan City Department of Environmental Protection received the complaint on the night of 22 April 2025. Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The bureau's own description is the only account of the system's contribution. The task force placed AI sound camera equipment at the relevant locations on the night of the complaint. Analysis of the noise data with the complaint reports gave the car's haunts and times. Environmental and police officers then found it near Daxing Road on 23 April. The sources do not say how the cameras tie noise to a vehicle. They report no decibel reading. They give no counterfactual for how long a conventional patrol would have taken. The stop, the referral and the pending penalty were the officers' work.

Its Quiet Taoyuan (靜桃) task force immediately set up AI sound camera equipment at the relevant spots. By analyzing the noise data against the complaints, it worked out where and when the car appeared. On 23 April environmental and police officers stopped it near Daxing Road. The car was referred to the motor vehicle office for a modification review. A Noise Control Act fine of up to NT$3,600 and an improvement order are to follow.

cases.reason: Detection, forecasting, or response to natural hazards.

details.label: Focus
details.value: Disaster warnings and response

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Crowd-sourced earthquake detection and early warning delivered to Android phones in countries without dense seismic networks. The alerts were the intended use.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: The system itself generated the detection and the alerts. A few hundred phones triggered on the P wave. The system detected the event 5.31 s after origin and issued alerts within 0.43 s. Magnitude estimates were updated over the next 12 s. All performance figures and user-response data come from Google-authored papers (Mousavi et al. 2026; Allen et al. 2025). That is said plainly here. The only independent cited source, the BBC, concerns the 2023 underestimation. The read papers describe the detection as an on-phone algorithm that analyzes acceleration time series for sudden changes. They do not use the terms machine learning or artificial intelligence. Whether the system uses AI is not established by the sources.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts detects the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake 5.31 s after origin and alerts over 16 million users on 23 April 2025; evaluation is Google-authored
record.summary: AEA detected the 23 April 2025 Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi quake in 5.31 s and alerted 16 million+ users (median 56 s warning for weak shaking); Google-authored evaluation; inland Take Action shortfall.
record.account: On 23 April 2025 the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at MMI V. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. Warning times for weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds with a median of 56 seconds. The authors report 90% true positives and 99% precision. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. The evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026) and the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) are written by Google employees. So is the user-feedback data. The same system underestimated the 6 February 2023 Türkiye earthquakes. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the M7.8 event. 10 million people could have received one.

data.retained_case_account: On 23 April 2025 the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at MMI V. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. Warning times for weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds with a median of 56 seconds. The authors report 90% true positives and 99% precision. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. The evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026) and the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) are written by Google employees. So is the user-feedback data. The same system underestimated the 6 February 2023 Türkiye earthquakes. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the M7.8 event. 10 million people could have received one.

fields.account: On 23 April 2025 the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at MMI V. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. Warning times for weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds with a median of 56 seconds. The authors report 90% true positives and 99% precision. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. The evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026) and the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) are written by Google employees. So is the user-feedback data. The same system underestimated the 6 February 2023 Türkiye earthquakes. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the M7.8 event. 10 million people could have received one.

fields.summary: AEA detected the 23 April 2025 Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi quake in 5.31 s and alerted 16 million+ users (median 56 s warning for weak shaking); Google-authored evaluation; inland Take Action shortfall.
fields.account: On 23 April 2025 the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at MMI V. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. Warning times for weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds with a median of 56 seconds. The authors report 90% true positives and 99% precision. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. The evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026) and the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) are written by Google employees. So is the user-feedback data. The same system underestimated the 6 February 2023 Türkiye earthquakes. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the M7.8 event. 10 million people could have received one.

record.title: Delhi Police matched a CCTV frame to a prior arrest record with Israeli facial recognition software, arrested two men within about a day of a Rs 80 lakh armed robbery in Chandni Chowk and recovered Rs 79.5 lakh
record.summary: Facial recognition on CCTV named a Chandni Chowk robber; two arrested within about a day and Rs 79.5 lakh of the Rs 80 lakh recovered.
record.account: On the evening of 17 March 2025, cash courier Ajmal Bhai Ganesh, 49, of R K Enterprises was robbed at gunpoint of Rs 80 lakh. It was near his Fatehpuri home, Chandni Chowk, Delhi. Delhi Police's North district analyzed some 500 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras' footage. Israeli facial recognition software matched a frame of a man who had followed the victim to a record at Kotwali police station. That gave Mohammad Ali, 21, of Daryaganj. Ali was arrested early on 19 March (the Times of India says Tuesday) and named Samir, 19, arrested in Daryaganj. A raid on Samir's home found Rs 79.5 lakh and a semi-automatic pistol, which police called the entire amount.

ratings.reason: Ajmal Bhai Ganesh and his employer R K Enterprises recovered Rs 79.5 lakh of the Rs 80 lakh taken at gunpoint. Police described that as the entire amount. A large material loss reversed within two days.
Delhi Police's North district cleared an armed robbery whose video had gone viral within about 24 hours. Both accused are in judicial custody under the BNS and Arms Act and the pistol recovered.
Two men who had surveilled cash couriers and used a firearm were taken off the street. The reports give no evidence of further robberies prevented, so the public benefit is small.

data.retained_case_account: On the evening of 17 March 2025, cash courier Ajmal Bhai Ganesh, 49, of R K Enterprises was robbed at gunpoint of Rs 80 lakh. It was near his Fatehpuri home, Chandni Chowk, Delhi. Delhi Police's North district analyzed some 500 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras' footage. Israeli facial recognition software matched a frame of a man who had followed the victim to a record at Kotwali police station. That gave Mohammad Ali, 21, of Daryaganj. Ali was arrested early on 19 March (the Times of India says Tuesday) and named Samir, 19, arrested in Daryaganj. A raid on Samir's home found Rs 79.5 lakh and a semi-automatic pistol, which police called the entire amount.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: By DCP (North) Raja Banthia's account, teams took a screengrab of a man seen following the victim. The Israeli software matched it to a prior record from Kotwali police station with a similarity score of 32.09 percent. That gave them Ali's name and his Daryaganj address. A score that low is a lead, not an identification. Police confirmed it by laying a trap and interrogating Ali. The auto-rickshaw trace, the reconnaissance evidence and Samir's arrest came from conventional work. The reports name neither the software nor its vendor.

record.account: Şırnak Provincial Police stopped a vehicle at the Köy Hizmetleri (Village Services) police checkpoint after ASENA selected it for inspection. DHA calls ASENA police software “in artificial intelligence format”. The narcotics dog Hector then found 86 kilograms 600 grams of skunk in 119 packages hidden in the trunk. Three occupants, M.E., H.K. and Ş.A., were detained (Sözcü/DHA and Habertürk/DHA, 17 March 2025). Diken, citing İHA, gives ASENA's full name as Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı (Narcotics Analysis Systems Network). It says the three were lawyers registered with the Mardin Bar Association. They were taken to court after police processing and remanded in custody (Diken, 18 March 2025). None of the reports gives the day of the stop, what data ASENA analyzed or how it chose the car, or any official's name.

data.retained_case_account: Şırnak Provincial Police stopped a vehicle at the Köy Hizmetleri (Village Services) police checkpoint after ASENA selected it for inspection. DHA calls ASENA police software “in artificial intelligence format”. The narcotics dog Hector then found 86 kilograms 600 grams of skunk in 119 packages hidden in the trunk. Three occupants, M.E., H.K. and Ş.A., were detained (Sözcü/DHA and Habertürk/DHA, 17 March 2025). Diken, citing İHA, gives ASENA's full name as Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı (Narcotics Analysis Systems Network). It says the three were lawyers registered with the Mardin Bar Association. They were taken to court after police processing and remanded in custody (Diken, 18 March 2025). None of the reports gives the day of the stop, what data ASENA analyzed or how it chose the car, or any official's name.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: ASENA supplied the selection and nothing more. DHA's wording is that the vehicle was identified and stopped “thanks to the ASENA software”. The dog Hector then found the packages and officers made the arrests. No report describes ASENA's inputs, its ranking method, or whether an analyst reviewed the flag before the stop.

details.value: Police facial recognition systems exist to identify people against identity and wanted-person records. Matching an unidentified detainee to a fugitive convict is that function, not a side effect.

details.value: The İHA and DHA reports credit the facial recognition system with the identification. record.title: A facial recognition check at an Adana police stop identified a man who said he had no ID as Süleyman Abül, a robbery convict wanted to serve a sentence of 10 years, 1 month and 10 days
record.summary: Adana police stopped a man with no ID; facial recognition identified him as a robbery convict wanted to serve a 10-year sentence.
record.account: Officers of the Seyhan District Police Directorate in Adana, Turkey, stopped a suspicious man during a street check in the Sucuzade neighborhood. He said he had no identity document and, by DHA's account, gave contradictory statements. So the district's Crime Prevention and Investigation Bureau took him to the station for fingerprint and facial recognition checks. The facial recognition system identified him as Süleyman Abül, 38, a fugitive convict wanted to serve 10 years, 1 month and 10 days for robbery. İHA and DHA published this in the early hours of 4 March 2025 without stating the day of the stop. The OECD Monitor dates it 3 March. DHA said he would go to prison once processing was done.
record.purpose: Police facial recognition systems exist to identify people against identity and wanted-person records. Matching an unidentified detainee to a fugitive convict is that function, not a side effect.

ratings.reason: The Seyhan unit established at the station that a man who said he had no ID and gave contradictory statements was a fugitive convict. He had a robbery sentence of 10 years, 1 month and 10 days outstanding, and could go to prison. A material but single-case gain for one police unit.
One convicted robber who had evaded a long sentence was returned to custody. The reports give no evidence of any further harm prevented, so the public benefit is small and diffuse.

data.retained_case_account: Officers of the Seyhan District Police Directorate in Adana, Turkey, stopped a suspicious man during a street check in the Sucuzade neighborhood. He said he had no identity document and, by DHA's account, gave contradictory statements. So the district's Crime Prevention and Investigation Bureau took him to the station for fingerprint and facial recognition checks. The facial recognition system identified him as Süleyman Abül, 38, a fugitive convict wanted to serve 10 years, 1 month and 10 days for robbery. İHA and DHA published this in the early hours of 4 March 2025 without stating the day of the stop. The OECD Monitor dates it 3 March. DHA said he would go to prison once processing was done.

details.value: Skylight's own account describes a two-stage AI contribution. A rule-based Speed Range Event flagged the vessel at under 6 knots inside an area of interest. 40 minutes later a Fishing Event from its machine-learning model, which detects longlining, trawling and squid jigging, reinforced the suspicion. record.title: Skylight speed-range and machine-learning fishing alerts may have led Argentina's Prefectura Naval to intercept the Vanuatu-flagged XINRUN 579 on 5 January 2025, and a fine may have been paid
record.summary: PNA intercepted XINRUN 579 fishing illegally in Argentina's EEZ on 5 January 2025; Skylight says its speed-range and ML fishing alerts prompted the response and a first electronic fine was paid.
record.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA) detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that as indicating trawling. Coastguard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, opening administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coastguard vessel. It led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence, with the fine and operational costs paid. It quotes the EICEMAR coordinator and the PNA GIS division lead crediting Skylight. The independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. The PNA release Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive. An NVIDIA Developer blog (3 March 2025) also reports the interdiction and fine.

data.retained_case_account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA) detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that as indicating trawling. Coastguard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, opening administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coastguard vessel. It led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence, with the fine and operational costs paid. It quotes the EICEMAR coordinator and the PNA GIS division lead crediting Skylight. The independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. The PNA release Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive. An NVIDIA Developer blog (3 March 2025) also reports the interdiction and fine.

PNA analysts then redirected a coastguard vessel. A retired PNA captain is quoted saying Skylight contributed directly to the decision. This is the maker's account, with the deployer's officers quoted inside it. The independent report (Agenda Malvinas, citing Pescare and official information) attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not name Skylight or AI. fields.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA) detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that as indicating trawling. Coastguard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, opening administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coastguard vessel. It led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence, with the fine and operational costs paid. It quotes the EICEMAR coordinator and the PNA GIS division lead crediting Skylight. The independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. The PNA release Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive. An NVIDIA Developer blog (3 March 2025) also reports the interdiction and fine.

fields.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA) detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that as indicating trawling. Coastguard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, opening administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coastguard vessel. It led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence, with the fine and operational costs paid. It quotes the EICEMAR coordinator and the PNA GIS division lead crediting Skylight. The independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. The PNA release Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive. An NVIDIA Developer blog (3 March 2025) also reports the interdiction and fine.

Analyst confirmation of each alert before dispatch

record.account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. Its final beta test in late October 2024 ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded and IoT devices. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target, generated and ran a fuzz test and exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer still referenced by a pointer. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in PR 8139 on 1 November 2024. It shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024, crediting “Peter” in the release notes. The vendor's blog post on the find is by engineer Peter Samarin.

fields.account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. Its final beta test in late October 2024 ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded and IoT devices. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target, generated and ran a fuzz test and exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer still referenced by a pointer. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in PR 8139 on 1 November 2024. It shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024, crediting “Peter” in the release notes. The vendor's blog post on the find is by engineer Peter Samarin.

ratings.reason: wolfSSL received a reproducible report of a heap use-after-free in a private-key parsing path. It merged the fix within days (PR 8139, 1 November 2024) and shipped it in 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024. The maintainers listed it among bug fixes rather than in the release's Vulnerabilities section. No CVE for it appears on wolfSSL's vulnerabilities page. The vendor itself says the exploit conditions “don't seem easy to meet”, so the benefit is material but bounded.

fields.summary: Spark, an AI fuzz-test agent, found a heap use-after-free in wolfSSL in late Oct 2024; fixed in PR 8139 and shipped in 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024.
fields.account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. Its final beta test in late October 2024 ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded and IoT devices. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target, generated and ran a fuzz test and exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer still referenced by a pointer. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in PR 8139 on 1 November 2024. It shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024, crediting “Peter” in the release notes. The vendor's blog post on the find is by engineer Peter Samarin.

record.title: Kunshan police “AI police” models flag a mobile gambling ring at Zhouzhuang, 20-plus arrested on 10 September 2024, and trace a telecom fraud's card transfers to freeze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes
record.summary: Kunshan police say their “AI police” models led a 10 September 2024 bust of a mobile gambling ring (20-plus arrests) and froze 500,000 yuan of a 980,000-yuan telecom fraud within 10 minutes.
record.account: On 10 September 2024, the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The models were built by the “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024. They report over 220 models and, over six months, 609 fraud cases solved and 32.47 million yuan recovered (both sources). All figures are the police's own.

data.retained_case_account: On 10 September 2024, the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The models were built by the “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024. They report over 220 models and, over six months, 609 fraud cases solved and 32.47 million yuan recovered (both sources). All figures are the police's own.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Both accounts are the police's. They credit the models with flagging the outdoor casino from behavioral features in bulk data and mapping the ring's structure “with one click”. They also traced card-tier fund flows in parallel, so a freeze came within 10 minutes. Officers made the arrests and freeze requests. Deputy criminal-investigation chief He Yongliang describes the gain as 24-hour, parallel rather than serial casework. Neither source separates the models' share from ordinary investigation.

fields.summary: Kunshan police say their “AI police” models led a 10 September 2024 bust of a mobile gambling ring (20-plus arrests) and froze 500,000 yuan of a 980,000-yuan telecom fraud within 10 minutes.
fields.account: On 10 September 2024, the Kunshan Public Security Bureau in Jiangsu broke up a gang running a mobile open-air casino in Zhouzhuang town. It arrested over 20 suspects. Modern Express reported that the “AI police” had found the ring (NetEase reprint, 6 October 2024). These are models that detect outdoor gambling from behavioral patterns in bulk data. In a telecom fraud handled by the Lujia police station, a victim lost 980,000 yuan. The models traced three tiers of card transfers and froze 500,000 yuan within 10 minutes. They identified 87 suspect accounts within 8 hours. Nine suspects were arrested on the third day with 200,000 yuan recovered (Suzhou Daily via suzhou.gov.cn, 7 October 2024). The models were built by the “Kunpeng Squad”, 35 officers assembled in May 2024. They report over 220 models and, over six months, 609 fraud cases solved and 32.47 million yuan recovered (both sources). All figures are the police's own.
