fields.account: ANSA reported on 14 Jul 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system. It is on the Rome-Naples high-speed line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. euronews (15 Jul 2025) added that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by an SDH fiber network. An advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the quake's danger, per euronews. The system had been operational since 3 May 2025. In the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. During it, trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. Neither article gives the date of that earthquake. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the system as AI-powered and a protective response.

produced_by: Dense accelerometric stations along a high-speed line in a seismic region
Low-latency fiber links to signaling
Automatic P-wave analysis with thresholds tied to train control
must_hold: P-waves arrive early enough before damaging shaking to brake trains
False triggers stay rare enough to keep the automatic stop enabled

record.summary: KTÜ students' AI quake app alerted phones about 30 s before a Kulu quake (DHA 5.2, USGS 5.0) was felt at Turkey's parliament, 15 May 2025.
record.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. DHA's report describes it as an AI-based earthquake early-warning system. During the presentation, in the TBMM Public Relations building in Ankara, a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital. DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2. USGS lists M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake. Students, some MPs and building staff went outside. The read reports mention no damage or injuries.

All four readable sources carry the same DHA report; ensonhaber.com and gercekgundem.com returned HTTP 403 and were not read. fields.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. DHA's report describes it as an AI-based earthquake early-warning system. During the presentation, in the TBMM Public Relations building in Ankara, a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital. DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2. USGS lists M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake. Students, some MPs and building staff went outside. The read reports mention no damage or injuries.

fields.account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center) to members of parliament. DHA's report describes it as an AI-based earthquake early-warning system. During the presentation, in the TBMM Public Relations building in Ankara, a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital. DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2. USGS lists M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake. Students, some MPs and building staff went outside. The read reports mention no damage or injuries.

details.label: Focus
details.value: Disaster warnings and response

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Built to detect earthquakes from the accelerometers of Android phones and combine the signals on Google's servers. It alerts users in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower seismic waves. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above. This alert was that intended function.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: If the reports are right, the alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake. Alerts were then pushed ahead of the slower waves, as Google's 2020 description and the 2025 Science paper set out. Google's own pages do not use the words AI or machine learning. The Science abstract speaks of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The OECD Monitor classifies the system as AI doing event detection. That alerts arrived seconds before shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets published within a day of the quake. None quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google. No Google per-event confirmation was found.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts reached phones in Crete and the Dodecanese seconds before the 14 May 2025 M6.0 (Greek press 6.1) Kasos quake
record.summary: Android users in Crete and the Dodecanese got Google's quake alert seconds before the M6.0 (Greek press 6.1) Kasos quake of 14 May 2025.
record.account: At 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May) a magnitude 6.0 (USGS; Greek outlets 6.1) earthquake struck. It struck 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, between Kasos and Karpathos, at 76 km depth. USGS logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported on 14 and 15 May on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System. In Europe it detects quakes from phone accelerometers rather than seismographs. It notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient, gives a lead time in seconds, or mentions damage or injuries.
record.purpose: Built to detect earthquakes from the accelerometers of Android phones and combine the signals on Google's servers. It alerts users in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower seismic waves. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above. This alert was that intended function.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth. A push alert could therefore outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese.

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection. In Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr).
Receiving phones with location (GPS) enabled and an internet connection, which Alphafreepress lists as requirements for the alerts
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.

later.note: Two months later Google's team published its Science evaluation of the Android system: over three years it delivered about 18 million alerts a month in 98 countries, and 36% of users who gave feedback received the alert before shaking (the paper does not discuss the Kasos event).
later.quote: Alerts were delivered in 98 countries for earthquakes with M ≥4.5, corresponding to ~60 events and 18 million alerts per month. User feedback shows that 85% of people receiving an alert felt shaking, and 36, 28, and 23% received the alert before, during, and after shaking, respectively.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Dated to 14 May 2025 local time: USGS gives the origin as 2025–05–13T22:51:15 UTC, M6.0 mww, 76 km depth, 20 km SSE of Fry, and in.gr places it in the early hours of Wednesday; Newsbomb's text says the early hours of Tuesday 13 May, which contradicts both and is not followed. Greek outlets report 6.1; USGS 6.0. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven as the classifier proposed. Of the Monitor's eight Greek sources, Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress state that users were alerted before the shaking (Newsbomb names Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away, by message and an audible signal like the 112 alert); Parapolitika is an explainer without that claim; eleftherostypos.gr and reader.gr returned HTTP 403 and ant1news.gr a TLS error, so they were not read. No Google statement about this event was found; web search was unavailable in this session, so sourcing is limited to the Monitor's list, USGS, Google's own pages and the Science abstract.
Benefit type set to Increased Product Safety under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Accessibility among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since from the cited sources.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.

data.retained_case_account: At 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May) a magnitude 6.0 (USGS; Greek outlets 6.1) earthquake struck. It struck 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, between Kasos and Karpathos, at 76 km depth. USGS logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported on 14 and 15 May on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System. In Europe it detects quakes from phone accelerometers rather than seismographs. It notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient, gives a lead time in seconds, or mentions damage or injuries.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: If the reports are right, the alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake. Alerts were then pushed ahead of the slower waves, as Google's 2020 description and the 2025 Science paper set out. Google's own pages do not use the words AI or machine learning. The Science abstract speaks of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The OECD Monitor classifies the system as AI doing event detection. That alerts arrived seconds before shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets published within a day of the quake. None quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google. No Google per-event confirmation was found.

fields.account: At 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May) a magnitude 6.0 (USGS; Greek outlets 6.1) earthquake struck. It struck 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, between Kasos and Karpathos, at 76 km depth. USGS logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported on 14 and 15 May on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System. In Europe it detects quakes from phone accelerometers rather than seismographs. It notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking. Notice came by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient, gives a lead time in seconds, or mentions damage or injuries.

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection. In Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr).

must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. The Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert.
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts). The feature must be supported in the region.

record.title: TrailGuard AI camera in Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary transmits images of armed poachers on two nights; Dudhwa Tiger Reserve officials identify them and investigate
record.summary: Dertien et al. (BioScience 2023): one TrailGuard AI unit captured poachers “carrying a gun and knives” on two dates and a poached chital; officials identified them. Arrests claimed only in releases.
record.account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The paper does not date the detections. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment. Poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found.
record.purpose: Built to detect tigers and people on trails with embedded AI and send real-time images to forest officials. Detecting and transmitting the poachers' images was that purpose.
record.system: TrailGuard AI camera-alert system (embedded AI on an Intel computer-vision chip; cellular transmission)
record.developer: Nightjar / RESOLVE, Washington DC (inventor Steve Gulick), with CVEDIA Ltd
record.deployer: Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh Forest Department, with the Global Tiger Forum, National Tiger Conservation Authority and Clemson University
record.location: Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary, Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh, India
record.taxonomy_note: The paper documents detection and identification of armed poachers for investigation, with arrests claimed only in releases, and the protected asset is wildlife.

ratings.reason: Forest officials received the images in near real time and identified the individuals. The paper documents an investigation, not an arrest or prosecution, so the recorded gain is an investigative lead.

Protection of the reserve's wildlife from this gang is claimed through arrests only in the Clemson release, developer material and The Hindu's second-hand report. The paper notes a chital presumably poached before the second detection.

data.retained_case_account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The paper does not date the detections. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment. Poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found.

fields.account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The paper does not date the detections. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment. Poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found.

fields.account: Dertien, Negi, Dinerstein and colleagues (BioScience 73(10):748–757, published online 14 September 2023) report deploying the TrailGuard AI camera-alert system. The paper does not date the detections. The system “runs on-the-edge artificial intelligence algorithms to detect tigers and poachers and transmit real-time images”. It was deployed in the Kanha-Pench corridor and in Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Uttar Pradesh. All seven Dudhwa units transmitted images; three transmitted objects of interest to forest department officials. “One unit within Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary captured a group of poachers carrying a gun and knives on two separate dates, and a presumably poached chital (Axis axis) on the second detection”. “Authorities were able to quickly identify the individuals via the transmitted images and were investigating the matter”. Tigers were detected at the same spot three days before the second poacher detection. The authors include RESOLVE and CVEDIA staff (the system's developers) alongside Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Wildlife Institute of India and Global Tiger Forum co-authors. AFP (Taipei Times, 6 October 2023) reported the study's claim of “identifying a team of poachers”. A Clemson University release of 15 September 2023 carries Nightjar/RESOLVE boilerplate. It states that the alerts “led the authorities to the arrest of these individuals for poaching a few weeks later”. It quotes Sanjay Kumar Pathak, former field director of Dudhwa, that the system “led to the detection and arrest of poachers in Dudhwa”. The Hindu (16 September 2023) cited a person involved in the experiment. Poachers caught on camera had a year later helped forest authorities secure a conviction. It quoted Piyush Yadav of Nightjar, the manufacturer, that “A year down, these poachers were arrested with images from TrailGuard playing a key role”. The article's lead puts the capture in Kanha-Pench and the Yadav quote in Dudhwa. No forest-department statement or court record of an arrest was found.

record.title: Meta threat alert, relayed through the FBI, brings Paraguayan police and psychologists to a bullied 17-year-old who praised the Uvalde shooter
record.summary: Meta flagged a Paraguayan teen's post praising the Uvalde shooter; the FBI relayed it and police, prosecutors and psychologists intervened.
record.account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter, called himself his “fan” and said something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative and was treated as a bullying victim. Police, prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists visited the home and recommended urgent psychological support, and also visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon or plan was reported.

data.retained_case_account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter, called himself his “fan” and said something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative and was treated as a bullying victim. Police, prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists visited the home and recommended urgent psychological support, and also visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon or plan was reported.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: Officials said the network detected the comment, classified it as dangerous and reported it. It went to the FBI and a 24/7 channel shared by prosecutors and the cybercrime police. Alarcón also spoke of corroborating “datos de analítica artificial” before the visit. No source says the flag was automated. Meta documents that its technology proactively detects most violating content before anyone reports it, but its referrals to law enforcement also pass through human review. Identifying the user, the home visit and the psychological support were the work of Paraguayan police, prosecutors and the child-protection office.

fields.summary: Meta flagged a Paraguayan teen's post praising the Uvalde shooter; the FBI relayed it and police, prosecutors and psychologists intervened.
fields.account: On Thursday 26 May 2022, two days after the Uvalde school shooting, Paraguay's Policía Nacional and Ministerio Público received an alert. It came from Meta's platform and the FBI office in Buenos Aires. A user in Paraguay had tagged the shooter, called himself his “fan” and said something similar could happen in Paraguay with more victims. Comisario Diosnel Alarcón's cybercrime department identified the Instagram profile as a 17-year-old in the “zona central”. He lived with a relative and was treated as a bullying victim. Police, prosecutors, the children's defender and psychologists visited the home and recommended urgent psychological support, and also visited a friend who knew of the posts. No weapon or plan was reported.

details.label: Focus
details.value: Disaster warnings and response

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Built to detect earthquakes from Android phones' accelerometers and alert users in the expected shaking zone seconds before the slower destructive waves arrive. It covers quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above. This alert was that intended function.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The OECD Monitor classifies it as an AI system doing event detection and forecasting, and the 2025 Science paper calls it smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

record.title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts reached Alanya phones seconds before the 5 January 2022 M5.1 (AFAD 5.3) Mediterranean quake
record.summary: Android users near Alanya, Turkey, got Google's earthquake alert seconds before a M5.1 (AFAD 5.3) offshore quake on 5 January 2022.
record.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

data.retained_case_account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The alert was produced end to end by Google's system. Accelerometer triggers from many phones were combined on Google's servers to detect the quake and estimate its size. Alerts were pushed to phones in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower S-waves. Google's own descriptions of this process do not use the words AI or machine learning. The OECD Monitor classifies it as an AI system doing event detection and forecasting, and the 2025 Science paper calls it smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms. The reported lead time varies by outlet (seconds, about 10 seconds, about one minute); Google promises seconds.

fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled

fields.summary: Android users near Alanya, Turkey, got Google's earthquake alert seconds before a M5.1 (AFAD 5.3) offshore quake on 5 January 2022.
fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

fields.account: At 06:21 local time on 5 January 2022 a magnitude 5.1 (USGS; AFAD 5.3) earthquake struck the Mediterranean about 57 km off Alanya, Antalya, Turkey. Depth: roughly 40 km. Yeni Şafak and DonanımHaber reported the same day on Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, introduced in Turkey in June 2021. It sent an audible and visual alert for a magnitude 5.3 quake to Android users seconds before the shaking. Hürriyet put the lead at about 10 seconds, while NTV and İndigo Dergisi claimed about a minute. AFAD and the Alanya district governor reported no damage or injuries. On 3 February 2022 Google said the system had alerted users to two January quakes centered on Alanya and Balıkesir.

produced_by: A magnitude 5.1 (AFAD 5.3) quake above the 4.5 alert threshold, centered about 57 km offshore and roughly 40 km deep. So the push alert could outrun the slower S-waves to the coast.

Enough Android phones near the epicenter with Earthquake Alerts on to trigger Google's server-side detection. Per Google's 3 February 2022 presentation it runs on Android 5.0 and later and users can switch it off.
Crowdsourced phone detection was the only input: Google partners with the ShakeAlert seismic network only in California, Oregon and Washington
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early. The 2025 Science paper reports only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking.
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice. Hürriyet reported on 7 January 2022 that most users who posted about the Alanya alert said they panicked
The phone must have location and the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled

record.account: UNEP’s MARS mitigation index lists eight Turkmenistan cases: two in Yelguyi in November 2024, Babarap in June 2025, Gugurtli field in July 2025, Balguyy in August 2025, two in Dauletabad in February 2026, and Lebap Province in March 2026. The available aggregate evidence does not isolate AI’s contribution from analysts, notifications, and physical repairs or quantify their combined benefit.

UNEP states that MARS combines satellite observations, scientific review, and AI to identify emissions for government and company action. The available aggregate evidence does not isolate AI’s contribution from analysts, notifications, and physical repairs or quantify their combined benefit.

record.title: Odakyu Electric Railway starts an AI crossing image-analysis system at four Odawara Line crossings that signals approaching trains to stop when people are left inside
record.summary: ITmedia (22 Jun 2026): from 24 Jun 2026 AI analyzes existing crossing cameras, tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, cyclists and motorcyclists and sends a brake signal to approaching trains; devel...
record.account: ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 Jun 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations, and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, not to identify individuals, and analysis data are destroyed within a year. The system was developed by Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries. It was trialed from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 Jun 2026. No detection events or outcomes are reported.

data.retained_case_account: ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 Jun 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations, and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, not to identify individuals, and analysis data are destroyed within a year. The system was developed by Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries. It was trialed from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 Jun 2026. No detection events or outcomes are reported.

fields.account: ITmedia's 岡田有花 reported on 22 Jun 2026 that Odakyu Electric Railway would introduce an “AI踏切画像解析システム” from 24 June 2026. It covers four crossings on its Odawara Line. They are Minami-Shinjuku Nos. 2, 4 and 5 between Minami-Shinjuku and Sangubashi stations, and Mukogaoka-Yuen No. 9 between Mukogaoka-Yuen and Ikuta stations. The AI analyzes footage from the existing safety-confirmation cameras in real time. It identifies and tracks pedestrians, wheelchair users, bicycles and motorcycles. When it detects someone left inside after the barriers come down, it sends a signal through the signaling equipment. That applies the brakes of approaching trains and lights the crossing's special signal lamps to alert crews. Both are released automatically once the crossing is clear. Images are used only for hazard detection, not to identify individuals, and analysis data are destroyed within a year. The system was developed by Meitetsu EI Engineer, Toyota Systems and Toho Electric Industries. It was trialed from January 2023, with work on detection accuracy at night and in rain. railf.jp carried the same announcement on 25 Jun 2026. No detection events or outcomes are reported.

record.account: Trade reports published on 15 and 16 Apr 2026 describe a study by the protection and indemnity insurer NorthStandard with Orca AI. The reports are MarineLink, Riviera Maritime Media's Martyn Wingrove, and Hellenic Shipping News reproducing Orca AI's release. The study covered a globally operating cohort of 139 container vessels fitted with Orca AI's navigation platform. Across more than 10.8 million nautical miles, it compared the first three months after installation with months 10 to 12. It reported a 52% reduction in high-severity close encounters, with 22% within the first six months. The reduction was 36% in the North and Baltic Seas and 18% in the seas around China and Japan. Encounters were defined by closest point of approach, time to closest point of approach, COLREGs interactions and traffic density. Orca AI's report page states that such encounters declined from 2.7 per vessel per month early after implementation to 1.3 by months 10 to 12. NorthStandard's head of loss prevention Colin Gillespie and Orca AI's chief executive Yarden Gross are quoted. The design is a before-and-after comparison on the same vessels with no control fleet, and the report is hosted by the vendor.

fields.account: Trade reports published on 15 and 16 Apr 2026 describe a study by the protection and indemnity insurer NorthStandard with Orca AI. The reports are MarineLink, Riviera Maritime Media's Martyn Wingrove, and Hellenic Shipping News reproducing Orca AI's release. The study covered a globally operating cohort of 139 container vessels fitted with Orca AI's navigation platform. Across more than 10.8 million nautical miles, it compared the first three months after installation with months 10 to 12. It reported a 52% reduction in high-severity close encounters, with 22% within the first six months. The reduction was 36% in the North and Baltic Seas and 18% in the seas around China and Japan. Encounters were defined by closest point of approach, time to closest point of approach, COLREGs interactions and traffic density. Orca AI's report page states that such encounters declined from 2.7 per vessel per month early after implementation to 1.3 by months 10 to 12. NorthStandard's head of loss prevention Colin Gillespie and Orca AI's chief executive Yarden Gross are quoted. The design is a before-and-after comparison on the same vessels with no control fleet, and the report is hosted by the vendor.

fields.account: Trade reports published on 15 and 16 Apr 2026 describe a study by the protection and indemnity insurer NorthStandard with Orca AI. The reports are MarineLink, Riviera Maritime Media's Martyn Wingrove, and Hellenic Shipping News reproducing Orca AI's release. The study covered a globally operating cohort of 139 container vessels fitted with Orca AI's navigation platform. Across more than 10.8 million nautical miles, it compared the first three months after installation with months 10 to 12. It reported a 52% reduction in high-severity close encounters, with 22% within the first six months. The reduction was 36% in the North and Baltic Seas and 18% in the seas around China and Japan. Encounters were defined by closest point of approach, time to closest point of approach, COLREGs interactions and traffic density. Orca AI's report page states that such encounters declined from 2.7 per vessel per month early after implementation to 1.3 by months 10 to 12. NorthStandard's head of loss prevention Colin Gillespie and Orca AI's chief executive Yarden Gross are quoted. The design is a before-and-after comparison on the same vessels with no control fleet, and the report is hosted by the vendor.

record.account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek says he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica says the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast last year. Politico calls the robots “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”.

The event lacks a verified location, date, unit, or casualty denominator, and the report describes current systems as remotely piloted. It does not establish that autonomous AI caused the result. The 22,000 missions cannot be converted into 22,000 lives saved, and lack of reported losses does not establish a net welfare effect.

Jacob Parakilas of RAND Europe writes in The Conversation that they are “mostly still remotely operated”. He says autonomy is limited to tasks such as highlighting identified enemy positions. The Debrief says it is unclear how much remote human control was involved at each stage. Politico separately notes a January 2026 case in which a DevDroid robot “equipped with artificial intelligence elements” took three prisoners, a different event.

fields.account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek says he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica says the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast last year. Politico calls the robots “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”.

details.value: Iron Beam is a high-energy laser built to intercept rockets, mortars and drones at short range. It is a low-cost complement to Iron Dome, David's Sling and Arrow. Interception of Hezbollah projectiles is its stated purpose.

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI or machine-learning system. Those sources are Ynet, JPost, Army Recognition, TimesNow, The Conversation and Moneycontrol. They also include Times of Israel 28 December 2025, 16 Mar, 27 Mar and 30 June 2026, and Wikipedia. They describe a high-power laser with a beam director and electro-optical targeting. The Monitor's “AI-enabled” label is its own. Rafael's CEO described machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). The IDF has not confirmed the engagement itself, so neither an AI role nor a contribution can be assessed.

record.title: Israel's Iron Beam laser may have made its first combat interception, of a Hezbollah drone, in footage of 2 March 2026
record.summary: Ynet and JPost (2 March 2026) call the video unconfirmed; Times of Israel (27 Mar, 30 June 2026) quotes officials that Iron Beam “has not yet been declared operational”. No cited source calls it AI.
record.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, not 28 February. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the IDF “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. The only confirmed laser combat use is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (JPost). The MoD said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only AI mention found is Rafael's CEO framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers.

data.retained_case_account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, not 28 February. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the IDF “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. The only confirmed laser combat use is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (JPost). The MoD said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only AI mention found is Rafael's CEO framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers.

fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, not 28 February. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the IDF “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. The only confirmed laser combat use is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (JPost). The MoD said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only AI mention found is Rafael's CEO framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers.

fields.summary: Ynet and JPost (2 March 2026) call the video unconfirmed; Times of Israel (27 Mar, 30 June 2026) quotes officials that Iron Beam “has not yet been declared operational”. No cited source calls it AI.
fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says that Israel “deployed its AI-powered Iron Beam laser defense system for the first time in combat to intercept Hezbollah missile barrages”. It separately bundles a Hankyoreh item (dated 10 October 2023) on Hamas rockets penetrating Iron Dome. The Iron Beam claim rests on social-media footage from Monday 2 March 2026, not 28 February. Ynet (Yair Kraus) reports that the footage “appeared to show the first operational use” of the system. It was delivered to the Israeli Air Force in late December 2025. Hezbollah fired rockets and drones from Lebanon after the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader, with one drone intercepted near Shlomi. The Jerusalem Post (Seth Frantzman, 2 March 2026) says that the circulated video “did not show lasers intercepting rockets”. TimesNow (2 March 2026) says that whether this was Iron Beam's first combat use “awaits official confirmation”. Army Recognition (3 March 2026) says that officials “have not formally confirmed the specific engagements” and that no authoritative combat log names the system. The Conversation (4 March 2026) calls the reports unconfirmed. Moneycontrol (3 March 2026) sources its “first-ever use” to an “Israel War Room” social-media video. The Times of Israel reports the Defense Ministry's handover of the first operational system on 28 December 2025, after tests against rockets, mortars and drones. Times of Israel/AFP (16 March 2026) reports that the IDF “has so far refused to comment on its use during the ongoing war”. Times of Israel (Stav Levaton, 27 March 2026) reports that “military officials said it has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian, 30 June 2026) reports that the one deployed system “has seen limited use and has not yet been declared operational within the IDF”. A senior officer called its coverage partial. The only confirmed laser combat use is aggregate and earlier. A lower-powered, shorter-range variant shot down some 35 drones from Lebanon in 2024 (Times of Israel/AFP). The Ministry of Defense announced it in May 2025 (JPost). The MoD said that no Iron Beam components were involved (Wikipedia). No cited source describes Iron Beam as an AI system. The only AI mention found is Rafael's CEO framing machine learning as a future capability (Breaking Defense, 22 October 2025). That piece is not among the sources. Metro, Economic Times, MoneyControl's second item, Hankyoreh and others among the Monitor's 20 listed sources are syndications or explainers.

record.account: Kyunghyang Shinmun's 최미랑 reported on 11 Feb 2026 that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport had drawn up a comprehensive railway-crossing accident-prevention plan. It was to take effect from March 2026. It includes an AI-based intelligent closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, to be installed in railway protection zones nationwide. The system immediately detects a vehicle or pedestrian trapped inside a crossing. It then transmits the information to the driver of an approaching train. Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The plan also adds fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period. They apply to vehicles that fail to stop or that enter while barriers operate. The ministry cited 36 crossing accidents over five years with 14 deaths and 7 injuries, 27 of them due to driver carelessness. No developer is named and no results exist. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor classified the announcement as an AI hazard rather than an incident.

data.retained_case_account: Kyunghyang Shinmun's 최미랑 reported on 11 Feb 2026 that the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport had drawn up a comprehensive railway-crossing accident-prevention plan. It was to take effect from March 2026. It includes an AI-based intelligent closed-circuit television (CCTV) system, to be installed in railway protection zones nationwide. The system immediately detects a vehicle or pedestrian trapped inside a crossing. It then transmits the information to the driver of an approaching train. Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The plan also adds fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period. They apply to vehicles that fail to stop or that enter while barriers operate. The ministry cited 36 crossing accidents over five years with 14 deaths and 7 injuries, 27 of them due to driver carelessness. No developer is named and no results exist. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor classified the announcement as an AI hazard rather than an incident.

Pilot installations were planned within the first quarter at Nonsan in Chungnam and at Boseong, where accidents occurred in 2025. Installation at the 543 national crossings would follow in sequence, depending on the results. The plan also adds fines of up to 70,000 won, after a six-month grace period. record.title: ProRail replaces 288 lineside cameras with AI “smart cameras” in 2026 and uses Genetec video analytics across 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to train dispatchers
record.summary: SpoorPro: ProRail swaps 288 lineside cameras for smart cameras in 2026, tests drones and runs Genetec video analytics on 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to dispatchers; no results are given.
record.account: SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new “smart” cameras. ProRail is also testing drones that fly autonomously and analyze images. ProRail is quoted that these forms of camera surveillance help it see and prevent incidents sooner, making the track safer with fewer disruptions and delays. The article's photo caption says the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7. The rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras it manages into one Genetec platform. It is monitored from ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room. Genetec Mission Control filters and analyzes alerts and forwards relevant images to an operator with suggested actions. Video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track). In that case the train dispatcher can warn drivers. The article quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. No source gives a detection count, a stopped train or a trespass reduction attributable to the analytics. No source on record identifies a UIC trespass-detection trial.

data.retained_case_account: SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new “smart” cameras. ProRail is also testing drones that fly autonomously and analyze images. ProRail is quoted that these forms of camera surveillance help it see and prevent incidents sooner, making the track safer with fewer disruptions and delays. The article's photo caption says the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7. The rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras it manages into one Genetec platform. It is monitored from ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room. Genetec Mission Control filters and analyzes alerts and forwards relevant images to an operator with suggested actions. Video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track). In that case the train dispatcher can warn drivers. The article quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. No source gives a detection count, a stopped train or a trespass reduction attributable to the analytics. No source on record identifies a UIC trespass-detection trial.

record.account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. That is a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. The entry states that the system has already recovered GH¢15 million from fraudulent importers. Its source is a GhanaWeb story titled “Government recovers GH¢15 million through new trade data system”. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm.

data.retained_case_account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. That is a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. The entry states that the system has already recovered GH¢15 million from fraudulent importers. Its source is a GhanaWeb story titled “Government recovers GH¢15 million through new trade data system”. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm.

fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry dated 16 January 2026 summarizes Ghanaian reports that the Ghana Revenue Authority launched Publican AI. That is a trade data analytics platform to identify customs fraud, undervaluation and falsified import documentation. The entry states that the system has already recovered GH¢15 million from fraudulent importers. Its source is a GhanaWeb story titled “Government recovers GH¢15 million through new trade data system”. The entry is classified as an AI Incident with the harm type economic harm to property interests. The Ghanaian Times (Kingsley Asare, 19 January 2026) reported remarks by Commissioner-General Dr Anthony Sarpong. He said that the Publican AI system would give 100 percent coverage of assessment. He said that assessments could be completed within five minutes instead of about two hours. He said that pilots showed 40–45% revenue gains. He said that rollout would begin at Tema Port on 1 February 2026. That article cites no realized recovery. The vendor is described only as a Cyprus-based firm.

record.account: MediaNama (Prabhanu Kumar Das) reported on 30 December 2025 on a Right to Information response. It showed 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 in August and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The tool was developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH). It analyzes transaction and account activity patterns across banks to identify accounts likely used as mules in financial fraud. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified or acted upon through MuleHunter.AI. The reason given was that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks and disclosure could harm competitive interests. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is reported as saying that the tool is showing a good success rate, without figures. RBIH's own project page was not available. News headlines from May to September 2026 describe an I4C-RBIH memorandum and deployment across 31 banks. The articles behind those headlines are not among the sources.

data.retained_case_account: MediaNama (Prabhanu Kumar Das) reported on 30 December 2025 on a Right to Information response. It showed 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 in August and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The tool was developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH). It analyzes transaction and account activity patterns across banks to identify accounts likely used as mules in financial fraud. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified or acted upon through MuleHunter.AI. The reason given was that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks and disclosure could harm competitive interests. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is reported as saying that the tool is showing a good success rate, without figures. RBIH's own project page was not available. News headlines from May to September 2026 describe an I4C-RBIH memorandum and deployment across 31 banks. The articles behind those headlines are not among the sources.

fields.summary: MediaNama's RTI (December 2025) found 23 banks had implemented RBIH's MuleHunter.AI, which analyzes transaction patterns to spot mule accounts; the RBI refused to release detection figures, citing ...
fields.account: MediaNama (Prabhanu Kumar Das) reported on 30 December 2025 on a Right to Information response. It showed 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 in August and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The tool was developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH). It analyzes transaction and account activity patterns across banks to identify accounts likely used as mules in financial fraud. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified or acted upon through MuleHunter.AI. The reason given was that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks and disclosure could harm competitive interests. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is reported as saying that the tool is showing a good success rate, without figures. RBIH's own project page was not available. News headlines from May to September 2026 describe an I4C-RBIH memorandum and deployment across 31 banks. The articles behind those headlines are not among the sources.

record.title: Open Climate Fix's Quartz Solar goes live in NESO's control room and may avoid £30m a year in imbalance costs
record.summary: Open Climate Fix's machine-learning solar forecast is live in NESO's control room; OCF claims at least £30m a year in avoided imbalance costs, a figure NESO's quoted statement does not give.
record.account: On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix (OCF), a not-for-profit, announced that Quartz Solar was live in the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) control room. OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure.

data.retained_case_account: On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix (OCF), a not-for-profit, announced that Quartz Solar was live in the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) control room. OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure.

fields.summary: Open Climate Fix's machine-learning solar forecast is live in NESO's control room; OCF claims at least £30m a year in avoided imbalance costs, a figure NESO's quoted statement does not give.
fields.account: On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix (OCF), a not-for-profit, announced that Quartz Solar was live in the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) control room. OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure.

record.summary: At DEF CON 33 (8 August 2025) DARPA reported seven teams' systems found 54 synthetic vulnerabilities, patched 43, and found 18 real bugs for disclosure; Team Atlanta won $4 million.
record.account: DARPA's results release describes the Final Competition. Teams' cyber reasoning systems tried to find and patch synthetic vulnerabilities across 54 million lines of real-world open-source code. They found 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities in 63 challenges and patched 43. They also found 18 real, non-synthetic vulnerabilities (six in C codebases, 12 in Java), now being responsibly disclosed. There were 11 patches for real bugs. The average cost was about $152 per task. Team Atlanta (Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, POSTECH) won $4 million, Trail of Bits $3 million and Theori $1.5 million. Four of seven systems were released open source. The Record reported the same figures from Las Vegas with program manager Andrew Carney's remarks. curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg, whose project was among the targets, examined the injected curl flaws. He judged them straightforward and not deeply hidden.

data.retained_case_account: DARPA's results release describes the Final Competition. Teams' cyber reasoning systems tried to find and patch synthetic vulnerabilities across 54 million lines of real-world open-source code. They found 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities in 63 challenges and patched 43. They also found 18 real, non-synthetic vulnerabilities (six in C codebases, 12 in Java), now being responsibly disclosed. There were 11 patches for real bugs. The average cost was about $152 per task. Team Atlanta (Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, POSTECH) won $4 million, Trail of Bits $3 million and Theori $1.5 million. Four of seven systems were released open source. The Record reported the same figures from Las Vegas with program manager Andrew Carney's remarks. curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg, whose project was among the targets, examined the injected curl flaws. He judged them straightforward and not deeply hidden.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: DARPA, the organizer, reports the figures. The Record corroborates from the event. Stenberg's independent look at the curl tasks suggests the injected flaws were easy. That bounds how much the synthetic scores show.

fields.summary: At DEF CON 33 (8 August 2025) DARPA reported seven teams' systems found 54 synthetic vulnerabilities, patched 43, and found 18 real bugs for disclosure; Team Atlanta won $4 million.
fields.account: DARPA's results release describes the Final Competition. Teams' cyber reasoning systems tried to find and patch synthetic vulnerabilities across 54 million lines of real-world open-source code. They found 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities in 63 challenges and patched 43. They also found 18 real, non-synthetic vulnerabilities (six in C codebases, 12 in Java), now being responsibly disclosed. There were 11 patches for real bugs. The average cost was about $152 per task. Team Atlanta (Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, POSTECH) won $4 million, Trail of Bits $3 million and Theori $1.5 million. Four of seven systems were released open source. The Record reported the same figures from Las Vegas with program manager Andrew Carney's remarks. curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg, whose project was among the targets, examined the injected curl flaws. He judged them straightforward and not deeply hidden.

record.title: India's DoT disconnects over 82 lakh mobile connections flagged by its AI facial-recognition tool ASTR
record.summary: DoT's indigenous ASTR tool matches subscriber photos to find connections taken by one person under different names; a Rajya Sabha reply (August 2025) counts more than 82 lakh disconnected after fai...
record.account: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, states that it designed and implemented ASTR. ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify and weed out fake, forged and non-bonafide mobile connections. A PIB Chennai release of 8 May 2023 reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. All were disconnected by operators, with point-of-sale details handed to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. The Hindu (PTI, 28 May 2023) quoted a senior DoT official in Patna. The official said that ASTR analysis found at least 21,800 connections exceeding the nine-per-subscriber limit in Bihar and Jharkhand. Around 17,000 of them were disconnected, and operators blacklisted 2,900 points of sale. Minister of State Dr Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar gave a Rajya Sabha written reply, posted by PIB on 7 August 2025. He said that DoT disconnected more than 82 lakh connections through ASTR after they failed re-verification. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the Bihar and Jharkhand deactivations as an AI Incident citing privacy, misidentification and data-protection concerns. The cumulative figure carries the reply's posting date. No independent accuracy evaluation was found.

data.retained_case_account: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, states that it designed and implemented ASTR. ASTR, the “AI and facial recognition powered Solution for Telecom SIM Subscriber Verification”, is to identify and weed out fake, forged and non-bonafide mobile connections. A PIB Chennai release of 8 May 2023 reported that ASTR identified more than 50,000 non-bonafide connections in Tamil Nadu. All were disconnected by operators, with point-of-sale details handed to the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing. The Hindu (PTI, 28 May 2023) quoted a senior DoT official in Patna. The official said that ASTR analysis found at least 21,800 connections exceeding the nine-per-subscriber limit in Bihar and Jharkhand. Around 17,000 of them were disconnected, and operators blacklisted 2,900 points of sale. Minister of State Dr Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar gave a Rajya Sabha written reply, posted by PIB on 7 August 2025. He said that DoT disconnected more than 82 lakh connections through ASTR after they failed re-verification. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the Bihar and Jharkhand deactivations as an AI Incident citing privacy, misidentification and data-protection concerns. The cumulative figure carries the reply's posting date. No independent accuracy evaluation was found.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: DoT describes ASTR as an indigenous AI and big-data analytic tool. It uses facial recognition to find connections taken by the same person under different names. Disconnection follows a failed re-verification step, so the tool flags connections rather than deciding. Developer and deployer are the same public body (DoT), which wrote the PIB releases.
