record.title: Philippine Red Cross activated its typhoon Early Action Protocol on 510's machine-learning impact forecast before Storm Nalgae (October 2022)
record.summary: 510 ML impact forecast hit the trigger on 27 October 2022; PRC installed shelter kits for 78 Aurora households before Storm Nalgae
record.account: The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) approved its Early Action Protocol (EAP) for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting (IBF) model, developed with 510 (Netherlands Red Cross), applies machine learning (ML) to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510/IBF forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That hit the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. With IFRC anticipatory DREF funds, PRC activated it in Aurora Province. On 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. PRC's post-storm survey reports all 78 kits installed, 390 people reached. CHF 7,002 of the CHF 117,555 budget was spent.

provenance.basis: Preserved from the existing AIBD record; external sources were not rechecked.

fields.account: The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) approved its Early Action Protocol (EAP) for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting (IBF) model, developed with 510 (Netherlands Red Cross), applies machine learning (ML) to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510/IBF forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That hit the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. With IFRC anticipatory DREF funds, PRC activated it in Aurora Province. On 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. PRC's post-storm survey reports all 78 kits installed, 390 people reached. CHF 7,002 of the CHF 117,555 budget was spent.

fields.account: The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) approved its Early Action Protocol (EAP) for typhoons in December 2019. Its impact-based forecasting (IBF) model, developed with 510 (Netherlands Red Cross), applies machine learning (ML) to predict housing damage per municipality from typhoon forecasts. As Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) approached on 27 October 2022, the 510/IBF forecast projected up to 10 percent shelter damage in priority municipalities. That hit the trigger at 56 hours' lead time. With IFRC anticipatory DREF funds, PRC activated it in Aurora Province. On 27 to 29 October, 40 workers distributed and installed shelter strengthening kits for 78 of 100 planned households in Dipaculao before landfall. PRC's post-storm survey reports all 78 kits installed, 390 people reached. CHF 7,002 of the CHF 117,555 budget was spent.

record.summary: Network Rail reported fewer trespass incidents after installing DeterTech AI cameras at Dingwall, alongside signage and campaigns. It supplied no post-installation count and noted a renewed rise.
record.account: Network Rail reported on June 9, 2026 that trespass had declined at Dingwall after it installed AI-powered DeterTech cameras. Monitoring in June 2025 had found an average of five incidents a day. The cameras detect people leaving the designated route, sound warnings, and send images to Network Rail and British Transport Police. Signage, safety campaigns, and minor site changes accompanied the installation. The release gives no post-installation count and says that incidents had begun rising again as the weather improved. It does not isolate the cameras’ effect or document an individual alert that prevented an accident.

record.summary: A vendor-affiliated CT study reported 86–96% detection of three marine-wildlife classes and 13% overall false alarms; testing used original scans and synthetic composites, with no customs outcome.
record.account: Pirotta and colleagues tested AI detection of marine wildlife in three-dimensional X-ray scans. Their June 8, 2026 paper reports 298 scans from 68 specimens, including preserved specimens and fresh shark material. The researchers expanded the scans by inserting specimen images into baggage images. A 512-bag test set contained both original scans and these synthetic composites, drawn from the same specimen population. Table 3 reports detection rates of 95% for shark fins, 96% for seahorses, and 86% for sea cucumbers. The overall false-alarm rate was 13%; the class-specific rates were 2%, 9%, and 1%. Rapiscan supplied equipment and funded staff participation in analysis and writing. The paper demonstrates laboratory detection, with no reported operational seizure or customs evaluation.

fields.account: Pirotta and colleagues tested AI detection of marine wildlife in three-dimensional X-ray scans. Their June 8, 2026 paper reports 298 scans from 68 specimens, including preserved specimens and fresh shark material. The researchers expanded the scans by inserting specimen images into baggage images. A 512-bag test set contained both original scans and these synthetic composites, drawn from the same specimen population. Table 3 reports detection rates of 95% for shark fins, 96% for seahorses, and 86% for sea cucumbers. The overall false-alarm rate was 13%; the class-specific rates were 2%, 9%, and 1%. Rapiscan supplied equipment and funded staff participation in analysis and writing. The paper demonstrates laboratory detection, with no reported operational seizure or customs evaluation.

record.title: Metropolitan Police announces exploration of AI to grade and triage child sexual abuse imagery to find unknown victims faster
record.summary: On 13 April 2026 the Met said it is exploring AI to grade and triage child sexual abuse imagery, testing with multiple companies, to flag unknown victims faster; no deployment or outcome yet.
record.account: The Metropolitan Police Service announced that it is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to support rapid grading and triage of child sexual abuse imagery. Material possibly relating to unknown victims could then be flagged for prioritized safeguarding. The force also wants to reduce officers' manual review of distressing material. It said it is in conversations with multiple companies and testing how this could work. It described a separate tool that reviews 641,000 messages in 35 minutes, and a £10 million investment in victim interview suites. It cited more than 5,400 child sexual abuse offenses investigated in the past year and over 1,300 children safeguarded. Deputy Commissioner Matt Jukes said speed matters for safeguarding and that human judgment and oversight would remain central. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records it as an “AI hazard”, noting the use is under consideration and not implemented.

data.retained_case_account: The Metropolitan Police Service announced that it is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to support rapid grading and triage of child sexual abuse imagery. Material possibly relating to unknown victims could then be flagged for prioritized safeguarding. The force also wants to reduce officers' manual review of distressing material. It said it is in conversations with multiple companies and testing how this could work. It described a separate tool that reviews 641,000 messages in 35 minutes, and a £10 million investment in victim interview suites. It cited more than 5,400 child sexual abuse offenses investigated in the past year and over 1,300 children safeguarded. Deputy Commissioner Matt Jukes said speed matters for safeguarding and that human judgment and oversight would remain central. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records it as an “AI hazard”, noting the use is under consideration and not implemented.

record.summary: NHC's 2025 verification: Google DeepMind ensemble mean beat official Atlantic track forecasts at 12–72 h; first AI models in NHC operations.
record.account: The National Hurricane Center's Forecast Verification Report for the 2025 season is dated 30 March 2026. It states that 2025 marked the first time NHC incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. In the Atlantic track comparison, the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly outperformed the official forecast at lead times from 12 to 72 h. Official forecasts outperformed the consensus aids TVCA, HCCA and FSSE. In the eastern North Pacific, GDMI performed considerably better than every other individual model. It beat the official forecast and all consensus aids at 48–120 h. For intensity it was the top individual model from 12 to 48 h. GDMI was not available early in the season, so the first storms are excluded from these comparisons.

data.retained_case_account: The National Hurricane Center's Forecast Verification Report for the 2025 season is dated 30 March 2026. It states that 2025 marked the first time NHC incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. In the Atlantic track comparison, the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly outperformed the official forecast at lead times from 12 to 72 h. Official forecasts outperformed the consensus aids TVCA, HCCA and FSSE. In the eastern North Pacific, GDMI performed considerably better than every other individual model. It beat the official forecast and all consensus aids at 48–120 h. For intensity it was the top individual model from 12 to 48 h. GDMI was not available early in the season, so the first storms are excluded from these comparisons.

record.title: wi.breathe cameras alert authorities to a Troizina wildfire, according to WINGS and the mayor
record.summary: WINGS and Troizinia-Methana’s mayor credit wi.breathe with an August 2025 wildfire alert. Contemporary reporting describes spread and a substantial firefighting response.
record.account: WINGS reported on September 2, 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected a wildfire in Troizina on August 28 and alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. No alert log, detection time, response chronology, or estimate of avoided damage accompanies that account. Contemporary reporting by Saronic Magazine describes the fire spreading uphill, hours of firefighting, precautionary evacuations, and damage to a shed. The municipality’s same-day statement credits a coordinated response involving more than 80 firefighters and six aircraft. Those accounts establish the scale of the fire and response, but neither verifies the AI’s contribution. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on May 12, 2026. The one-minute detection figure in circulated completion publicity is a capability claim, not a measured result for the August fire.

data.retained_case_account: WINGS reported on September 2, 2025 that its wi.breathe cameras in Methana had detected a wildfire in Troizina on August 28 and alerted authorities. The company quoted Mayor Tasos Ath. Mougios crediting the system with preventing a larger disaster. No alert log, detection time, response chronology, or estimate of avoided damage accompanies that account. Contemporary reporting by Saronic Magazine describes the fire spreading uphill, hours of firefighting, precautionary evacuations, and damage to a shed. The municipality’s same-day statement credits a coordinated response involving more than 80 firefighters and six aircraft. Those accounts establish the scale of the fire and response, but neither verifies the AI’s contribution. WINGS later announced completion of the wider camera installation on May 12, 2026. The one-minute detection figure in circulated completion publicity is a capability claim, not a measured result for the August fire.

record.title: UNDP hands SESU the Ukrainian “Mines Eye” AI aerial detection system after a pilot that scanned over 360 hectares in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts
record.summary: Mines Eye (magnetometry, visual/infrared imaging, AI detection of explosive remnants) scanned over 360 ha in a five-month SESU pilot; handed over 21 June 2025. No detection or land-release counts.
record.account: UNDP Ukraine's press release of 21 June 2025 is datelined Mykolaiv. It says UNDP “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)”. Financial support came from the Government of Luxembourg. The base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast hosted it, with UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu present. The release calls the system “Developed in Ukraine” but does not name the developer. It combines magnetometry with visual and infrared aerial imaging. It states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”. It produces maps and anomaly reports for operators before manual or mechanical clearance. UNDP-trained SESU teams ran a five-month pilot. They “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. The release gives no number of items detected or confirmed, no hectares released, and no accuracy figure. UNDP's 26 June 2025 release concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No source independent of UNDP or SESU was found.

data.retained_case_account: UNDP Ukraine's press release of 21 June 2025 is datelined Mykolaiv. It says UNDP “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)”. Financial support came from the Government of Luxembourg. The base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast hosted it, with UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu present. The release calls the system “Developed in Ukraine” but does not name the developer. It combines magnetometry with visual and infrared aerial imaging. It states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”. It produces maps and anomaly reports for operators before manual or mechanical clearance. UNDP-trained SESU teams ran a five-month pilot. They “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. The release gives no number of items detected or confirmed, no hectares released, and no accuracy figure. UNDP's 26 June 2025 release concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No source independent of UNDP or SESU was found.

fields.account: UNDP Ukraine's press release of 21 June 2025 is datelined Mykolaiv. It says UNDP “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)”. Financial support came from the Government of Luxembourg. The base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast hosted it, with UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu present. The release calls the system “Developed in Ukraine” but does not name the developer. It combines magnetometry with visual and infrared aerial imaging. It states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”. It produces maps and anomaly reports for operators before manual or mechanical clearance. UNDP-trained SESU teams ran a five-month pilot. They “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. The release gives no number of items detected or confirmed, no hectares released, and no accuracy figure. UNDP's 26 June 2025 release concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No source independent of UNDP or SESU was found.

record.title: Austin Energy deploys 13 Pano AI wildfire cameras across its 437-square-mile territory
record.summary: The City of Austin's utility announced full deployment of a 13-camera Pano AI detection system covering its service area with the Austin Fire Department (29 August 2024); no detections are reported.
record.account: Austin Energy, the City of Austin's electric utility, announced the full deployment of a Pano AI system on 29 August 2024. It combines 13 ultra-high-definition 360-degree cameras, artificial intelligence and real-time monitoring across its 437-square-mile service territory. It covers most of Travis County and parts of Hays, Bastrop, Williamson and Burnet counties. Once a fire is identified the system alerts Austin Energy and local fire departments with location data and imagery. The utility says it supports decisions such as power shut-offs. Wildfire program manager Chris Vetromile and Austin Fire Department wildfire mitigation officer Justice Jones are quoted. Pano AI's Arvind Satyam is also quoted. The release reports no detection or contained fire. The source is the deployer's own announcement (a public body), with the vendor quoted inside it. No independent report is among the sources.

It covers most of Travis County and parts of Hays, Bastrop, Williamson and Burnet counties. Once a fire is identified the system alerts Austin Energy and local fire departments with location data and imagery. The utility says it supports decisions such as power shut-offs. Wildfire program manager Chris Vetromile and Austin Fire Department wildfire mitigation officer Justice Jones are quoted. Pano AI's Arvind Satyam is also quoted. The release reports no detection or contained fire. The source is the deployer's own announcement (a public body), with the vendor quoted inside it. No independent report is among the sources.

fields.account: Austin Energy, the City of Austin's electric utility, announced the full deployment of a Pano AI system on 29 August 2024. It combines 13 ultra-high-definition 360-degree cameras, artificial intelligence and real-time monitoring across its 437-square-mile service territory. It covers most of Travis County and parts of Hays, Bastrop, Williamson and Burnet counties. Once a fire is identified the system alerts Austin Energy and local fire departments with location data and imagery. The utility says it supports decisions such as power shut-offs. Wildfire program manager Chris Vetromile and Austin Fire Department wildfire mitigation officer Justice Jones are quoted. Pano AI's Arvind Satyam is also quoted. The release reports no detection or contained fire. The source is the deployer's own announcement (a public body), with the vendor quoted inside it. No independent report is among the sources.

record.title: Germany tests IdentiFlight cameras for bird protection
record.summary: An OECD entry reports German deployment in September 2022. OekoFor's undated firsthand account describes German test-site validation, without a measured reduction in bird fatalities.
record.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry summarizes press coverage of 20 and 21 September 2022 (The Guardian, Mother Jones, The Register and others, not among the sources). It says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight to detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines and slow the blades to prevent collisions. The monitor's rationale cites the 82% reduction reported from the Wyoming study rather than a German measurement. OekoFor's undated page, also retained among the sources, describes IdentiFlight systems installed at German test sites. OekoFor and ARSU supervise validation that compares the systems' observations with ornithologists' reference data. The undated page does not establish when those tests began or supply a German fatality-reduction estimate.
record.purpose: IdentiFlight is built to detect eagles and curtail turbines; protecting lesser spotted eagles at German wind farms is the intended use.
record.system: IdentiFlight automated eagle detection and turbine curtailment

details.label: AI contribution
details.value: OCHA's 2021, 2023 and 2025 frameworks name the IFRC/510 impact model as the activation-trigger model. The 2021 framework describes it as partially a machine learning model. This is documented by the deployer, not only the maker. The model's forecasts were monitored during the December 2021 near activation (Typhoon Rai) without meeting criteria. The 2024 readiness phase for Pepito ended with CERF AA resources reallocated to response. OCHA's flash update attributes the 6 November 2025 activation for Uwan to the observational threshold (forecast peak 195 km/h against the 185 km/h trigger). It does not state that the 510 model's estimates reached the activation matrix. The AI's contribution to any payout is therefore not established. The maker's NHESS paper is the only source describing the algorithm (XGBoost).

record.title: UN OCHA's CERF anticipatory action framework for Philippine typhoons adopted 510's machine-learning impact model as trigger in 2021; no activation on that trigger documented to 2025
record.summary: OCHA frameworks (2021, 2023, 2025) use 510's XGBoost house-damage model as activation trigger; near-activation Dec 2021 (Rai); the Nov 2025 activation for Uwan ran on the 185 km/h wind trigger.
record.account: OCHA's Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons was posted on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million CERF pilot for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model's predicted number of totally damaged houses. The framework says that model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. 510's 2024 NHESS paper (vendor-authored) states the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. It adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. OCHA's June 2025 report says the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports nearly US$6 million released and WFP alone reaching 42,100 families. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.

ECMWF ensemble track, wind and rainfall forecasts fed to the 510 impact model every 6–12 hours
Historical house-damage data linking hazard, vulnerability and exposure to train the model

must_hold: Forecast lead time of at least 72 hours; rapid intensification (Rai 2021) shortened lead time below the trigger window
Model impact estimates reaching the regional threshold matrix, which no read activation record documents
Agency delivery capacity (financial service providers, data-sharing agreements) in the 72 hours before landfall
PAGASA and ECMWF data availability

data.retained_case_account: OCHA's Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons was posted on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million CERF pilot for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model's predicted number of totally damaged houses. The framework says that model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. 510's 2024 NHESS paper (vendor-authored) states the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. It adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. OCHA's June 2025 report says the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports nearly US$6 million released and WFP alone reaching 42,100 families. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.

fields.account: OCHA's Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons was posted on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million CERF pilot for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model's predicted number of totally damaged houses. The framework says that model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. 510's 2024 NHESS paper (vendor-authored) states the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. It adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. OCHA's June 2025 report says the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports nearly US$6 million released and WFP alone reaching 42,100 families. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.

fields.summary: OCHA frameworks (2021, 2023, 2025) use 510's XGBoost house-damage model as activation trigger; near-activation Dec 2021 (Rai); the Nov 2025 activation for Uwan ran on the 185 km/h wind trigger.
fields.account: OCHA's Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons was posted on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million CERF pilot for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model's predicted number of totally damaged houses. The framework says that model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. 510's 2024 NHESS paper (vendor-authored) states the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. It adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. OCHA's June 2025 report says the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports nearly US$6 million released and WFP alone reaching 42,100 families. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.

details.value: No cited source documents an AI or machine-learning role. INTERPOL's release says it tracked the vessel with support from OceanMind and that hourly updates were aided by contributions from Global Fishing Watch. GFW's own article credits named analysts who tracked AIS data, predicted the course and identified rendezvous points. It does not mention algorithms, machine learning or automated detection. OceanMind's homepage states only that it uses satellites, AI and human expertise in general. The AI role is thus undocumented rather than established. The account comes from INTERPOL, GFW, and the Blue Belt blog. The court outcome (Supreme Court verdict of 27 February 2020, conviction, Rp300,000,000 fine, forfeiture) comes from the Blue Belt blog. The Blue Belt post of 5 June 2021 is no longer available, and no archived copy is cited.

record.title: Indonesia captures the blacklisted MV NIKA on 12 July 2019 after INTERPOL tracking supported by OceanMind and Global Fishing Watch; the tracking was by analysts, not an AI detection
record.summary: MV NIKA seized by Indonesia 12 July 2019 after INTERPOL tracking with OceanMind and GFW; captain convicted, owner fined, vessel forfeited; no cited source documents an AI detection.
record.account: INTERPOL reported on 22 July 2019 that the MV NIKA had been detained by Indonesian authorities. The vessel was suspected of illegal fishing in the Southern Ocean. Its owner also owned the blacklisted STS 50 intercepted in Indonesia in 2018. INTERPOL tracked the vessel's movement with support from the UK not-for-profit OceanMind, sending daily reports to Indonesia, New Zealand, Panama, the UK and the US. Hourly updates aided by Global Fishing Watch (GFW) followed as it approached Indonesian waters. GFW's account (23 July 2019) says GFW analyst Imam Prakoso helped track the vessel from February 2019 after it illegally switched off its tracking system. It says a live multi-way communication between Indonesian naval and fishery officials, INTERPOL and GFW analyst Charles Kilgour exchanged information. GFW analysts helped predict its course and identify rendezvous points. Indonesian patrol boats ORCA 2 and ORCA 3 intercepted it on 12 July 2019 at 08:06 local time. The court outcome comes from a UK Government Blue Belt blog of 5 June 2021. That blog was no longer available as of 20 October 2026. The Indonesian Supreme Court gave its verdict on 27 February 2020, the captain was convicted, the owner fined Rp300,000,000 and the vessel forfeited. None of the sources describes a machine-learning or AI detection. OceanMind's homepage says only, in general terms, that it uses satellites, AI and human expertise.

data.retained_case_account: INTERPOL reported on 22 July 2019 that the MV NIKA had been detained by Indonesian authorities. The vessel was suspected of illegal fishing in the Southern Ocean. Its owner also owned the blacklisted STS 50 intercepted in Indonesia in 2018. INTERPOL tracked the vessel's movement with support from the UK not-for-profit OceanMind, sending daily reports to Indonesia, New Zealand, Panama, the UK and the US. Hourly updates aided by Global Fishing Watch (GFW) followed as it approached Indonesian waters. GFW's account (23 July 2019) says GFW analyst Imam Prakoso helped track the vessel from February 2019 after it illegally switched off its tracking system. It says a live multi-way communication between Indonesian naval and fishery officials, INTERPOL and GFW analyst Charles Kilgour exchanged information. GFW analysts helped predict its course and identify rendezvous points. Indonesian patrol boats ORCA 2 and ORCA 3 intercepted it on 12 July 2019 at 08:06 local time. The court outcome comes from a UK Government Blue Belt blog of 5 June 2021. That blog was no longer available as of 20 October 2026. The Indonesian Supreme Court gave its verdict on 27 February 2020, the captain was convicted, the owner fined Rp300,000,000 and the vessel forfeited. None of the sources describes a machine-learning or AI detection. OceanMind's homepage says only, in general terms, that it uses satellites, AI and human expertise.

record.summary: CMS's return-on-investment report for the Fraud Prevention System's fourth implementation year counts $654.8 million in inappropriate Medicare payments identified or prevented in 2015 against $57.1...
record.account: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services' report “Fraud Prevention System Return on Investment, Fourth Implementation Year” is undated. The Wayback Machine archived it on 24 August 2016. It states the FPS helped identify or prevent $654.8 million in inappropriate payments during calendar year 2015, about 44% more than the previous year. That counts actions taken due to the FPS and investigations it expedited, augmented or corroborated. The corrected ROI is $11.5 to $1, after a rounding error in the originally reported $11.6. Table 1 trends identified savings from $115.4 million in the first year (July 2011 to June 2012) through $250.1 million and $454.0 million. The cumulative total is $1,474.3 million. Savings are split across pre-payment edit denials, payment suspensions, projected cost avoidance from revoking billing privileges and overpayments referred for recovery. The value of law-enforcement referrals was $49.2 million in 2015. The report says the methodology was certified by the HHS Office of Inspector General. It puts 45 providers on active payment suspension at year end. Costs were an estimated $57.1 million, including $19.5 million for a developing contractor and $4.8 million for a modeling contractor. The report does not describe the system's technique.

data.retained_case_account: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services' report “Fraud Prevention System Return on Investment, Fourth Implementation Year” is undated. The Wayback Machine archived it on 24 August 2016. It states the FPS helped identify or prevent $654.8 million in inappropriate payments during calendar year 2015, about 44% more than the previous year. That counts actions taken due to the FPS and investigations it expedited, augmented or corroborated. The corrected ROI is $11.5 to $1, after a rounding error in the originally reported $11.6. Table 1 trends identified savings from $115.4 million in the first year (July 2011 to June 2012) through $250.1 million and $454.0 million. The cumulative total is $1,474.3 million. Savings are split across pre-payment edit denials, payment suspensions, projected cost avoidance from revoking billing privileges and overpayments referred for recovery. The value of law-enforcement referrals was $49.2 million in 2015. The report says the methodology was certified by the HHS Office of Inspector General. It puts 45 providers on active payment suspension at year end. Costs were an estimated $57.1 million, including $19.5 million for a developing contractor and $4.8 million for a modeling contractor. The report does not describe the system's technique.

fields.account: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services' report “Fraud Prevention System Return on Investment, Fourth Implementation Year” is undated. The Wayback Machine archived it on 24 August 2016. It states the FPS helped identify or prevent $654.8 million in inappropriate payments during calendar year 2015, about 44% more than the previous year. That counts actions taken due to the FPS and investigations it expedited, augmented or corroborated. The corrected ROI is $11.5 to $1, after a rounding error in the originally reported $11.6. Table 1 trends identified savings from $115.4 million in the first year (July 2011 to June 2012) through $250.1 million and $454.0 million. The cumulative total is $1,474.3 million. Savings are split across pre-payment edit denials, payment suspensions, projected cost avoidance from revoking billing privileges and overpayments referred for recovery. The value of law-enforcement referrals was $49.2 million in 2015. The report says the methodology was certified by the HHS Office of Inspector General. It puts 45 providers on active payment suspension at year end. Costs were an estimated $57.1 million, including $19.5 million for a developing contractor and $4.8 million for a modeling contractor. The report does not describe the system's technique.
